Title: The Swiss Franc within an Euro Environment
text: The Swiss Franc within an Euro Environment Address given by Jean-Pierre Roth Vice-Chairman of the Governing Board Swiss National Bank On the occasion of the 12th European Finance Convention and the Euro Week Vienna, 23 November, 1998 2 It is a great pleasure for me to be here, in this beautiful city of Vienna, the present capital of the European Union. The venue of this conference could not have been better chosen. In just a few weeks, Europe will take the historic step of monetary integration. On this particular occasion, I am especially honoured to address such a gathering of central bank officials, representatives of finance ministries and commercial bankers, and to offer you the views of the Swiss National Bank (SNB) on the monetary challenges ahead. As you are well aware, Switzerland, like a few other European countries, will not be integrated in the future Monetary Union. Its position outside  Euroland  is the logical consequence of its political decision not to adhere to the European Union for the time being. For all Europeans, the most visible short-term consequence of the Monetary Union will be the new central bank architecture and the creation of the euro. On January 1st, the national central banks will merge in the System of European Central Banks where monetary sovereignty is to be exercised, and banks will be allowed to denominate deposits in euros. In future, the ECB will be in charge of the monetary management of Euroland, a zone as large as the United States. Euroland will be a vast market without exchange rate risks in domestic transactions. Although Switzerland will remain outside the euro area, it will also be affected by the revolution produced by the single currency. I use the word  revolution  here to stress how deep and far-reaching the final impact of the euro will be, and also to show up the uncertain implications of the introduction of the common currency. The Monetary Union is a big step forward, but it is a big step in the dark ! We all expect that the single currency will enhance transparency on the EU market for goods and services, and we believe that it will be a tremendous integration factor on the European capital market. No doubt, the euro will stimulate competition among producers and create a new framework for the banking and financial industry. But, like in any revolutionary situation, there will be considerable uncertainties following the introduction of the euro, especially uncertainties surrounding the structural impact of the common currency in the long run. 3 All Europeans have to live with these uncertainties, whether they have decided or not to join the union. In our case we know that the Swiss franc will remain an independent currency. We also realise that our country will be totally surrounded by the euro zone. What kind of impact can we expect for our economy, what challenges will it represent for monetary policy ? 1. The impact on the Swiss economy For Switzerland, the unification of the European monetary landscape is basically excellent news. For the first time in our history we will be located in the middle of a large monetary zone where price stability will be the objective of monetary policy. Why is it good news ? Because Switzerland always had to go through painful adjustments whenever any of its trading partners were afflicted by monetary disorders. It is not necessary to go back as far as the 19th century or even the 1930s to be convinced of the perverse impact of large currency fluctuations or competitive devaluations. Even during the 1990s, the marked weakening of the Italian lira created a major problem for us, especially for our textile industry and for the south of Switzerland, where relations with Italy are traditionally very close. If, tomorrow, the euro provides Europe with a stable currency, this will not only be profitable for the participating countries, but it will also be in the interests of small countries such as Switzerland. 70% of our imports come from Euroland, which, in turn, absorbs more than half of our exports. The main issue facing non-participating countries is the issue of the stability of the euro. Here again, we have little to go by because the value of the euro will depend on the future policy adopted by the ECB. We have good reason to believe that the relationship between the euro and the Swiss franc will be stable. 4  First, the objective of monetary policy of the ECB coincides perfectly with our own policy orientation towards price stability. The fact that the ECB will be an independent central bank is a further factor in favour of a stable policy.  Secondly, our experience of more than 25 years of currency floating shows that with converging fundamentals and similar policy objectives, there is a good chance that the exchange rate relations between Euroland and Switzerland will remain within an acceptable fluctuation band. It is striking to see how relatively stable a flexible Swiss franc (measured in real terms) has been vis-a-vis the German mark. From 1983 to 1998, our currency has strengthened yearly at the low rate of 0.5% vis-a-vis the mark and fluctuated within a band of /- 5%. These results, which have been achieved by market forces alone since the SNB did not intervene in the foreign exchange market, produced a situation of a quasi-fixed exchange rate. At least, they do not give the impression that the foreign exchange market has been behaving irrationally in contradiction to the fundamentals of the respective countries. This stability demonstrates that two countries having the same policy objectives, similar inflation rates and strongly correlated business cycles can enjoy a relatively stable bilateral exchange rate. The bottom line of this is clear : the more Switzerland behaves like a European country, the greater the chance of currency stability between the Swiss franc and the euro. We are thus confident that the absence of major tensions observable over the last two years will be an enduring phenomenon and that the market will gradually come to recognise that the Swiss franc and the euro are two currencies belonging to the same European family. The exchange rate is not the only channel through which the single currency will have an impact on our economy. With more homogeneity in the monetary landscape, the position of the Swiss franc as a transaction currency could weaken. All the ingredients are there for Euroland to become progressively a large domestic market where transactions in foreign currencies could represent only a small portion of the exchanges on the market. As we know that small economies trading with large markets have to adjust to the conditions imposed by their larger partners, 5 Switzerland can be expected to make less use of the Swiss franc as a means of payment in its foreign trade than in the past. We can also envisage Swiss exporters themselves being fascinated by the advantages of operating in euros. They will have an incentive to keep their books in euros and to balance their revenues in euros by covering expenses in euros in order to eliminate exchange risks as far as possible. It is not even excluded that domestic producers will be forced to offer euro conditions in order to remain competitive as intermediate suppliers. Labour costs will however remain an irreducible part of domestic production costs. Equally, we can expect the euro to be widely used for payments in Switzerland. Europeans will see the euro as an excellent instrument of efficient cash management. Soon the euro could become the vehicle currency in Europe. Travellers will find it easier to pay in euros instead of using other currencies. As a first step, euro payments will take the form of transfers of electronic money, then payments will ensue in euro banknotes. Switzerland is taking the necessary steps for dealing with payments in foreign currencies. All this requires a careful preparation of processing procedures and a close technical integration in the European payment system. Our banks have invested a great deal of time and money in preparing themselves to supply financial services in euros. Starting next year, they will clear their euro transactions through a special clearing institution established in Frankfurt and linked to the ECB. It will then be possible to carry out transactions in euros in Switzerland as efficiently as in the EU countries. Given the very close relations between Switzerland and Euroland, the exchange rate sensitivity of the Swiss economy is expected to increase, which will require not only an efficient clearing system but also a tight management of exchange rate risks at all levels. 6 2. A challenge for monetary policy I opened my speech by stressing the revolutionary aspect of the euro. The single currency will profoundly change the European monetary landscape and will affect not only the EU but also the countries remaining outside the Union. Switzerland, with its central position and its close economic and financial relations with its neighbours, will be particularly affected. This, of course, will create a new framework for monetary policy. Switzerland traditionally implements an independent monetary policy. Since the breakdown of the Bretton Woods system in 1973, the Swiss franc has been floating, and the SNB's policy has aimed at price stability. From the outset, a considerable convergence of monetary policy objectives will exist between the SNB and the future European central bank. This is of major importance. As I mentioned earlier on, experience shows that countries with similar policy objectives and converging fundamentals usually enjoy stable exchange rates. We can thus believe that, over time, the markets will realise that the Swiss franc and the euro are currencies with similar characteristics. If that is so, why do we not change our monetary strategy, why do we not set a parity between the Swiss franc and the euro, following the policy pursued by Austria before the Schilling joined the European Monetary System ? There are voices in Switzerland asking for a return to an official fixed exchange rate regime or, at least, that the Swiss National Bank stabilises the external value of the Swiss franc in order to reduce uncertainty surrounding the value of the Swiss franc on the market, uncertainty which imposes hedging costs on our exporters. Unfortunately, the implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime is not a feasible alternative for the time being. Why not ? If we set a parity for the Swiss franc, this would be an autonomous decision which would not necessarily be taken as irrevocable by the markets. A fixed exchange rate strategy must be totally credible in order to play its stabilising role. If the market had any suspicion that the Swiss franc might be revalued in the future, the risk of 7 speculative attacks against the declared parity would be considerable. As long as Switzerland is not a member of the European Union, it will be difficult to convince the market that any parity of the Swiss franc will never be adjusted. Any attempt to set a parity would thus stimulate speculation instead of calming it down. It is therefore in our interest to maintain a flexible relation between the Swiss franc and the euro. But we also have to recognise that, with relatively low interest rates, Switzerland has no incentive, for the time being, to create a strong link between the Swiss franc and the euro. If the markets were to believe that the exchange rate risk between the euro and the Swiss franc is negligible, our interest rates would move rapidly towards the euro rates, and this would have a negative impact on aggregate demand in Switzerland, especially on investment and housing. Here again, flexibility of the exchange rate is of the essence. Having said that, Ladies and Gentlemen, we do not exclude the possibility of intervening in the foreign exchange market or on the money market in order to fight against exchange rate developments which could be considered out of line with economic fundamentals. A relaxation of monetary policy in reaction to pressures on the Swiss franc is a clear option. Flexibility in the conduct of monetary policy as an answer to market instability has been our strategy over the last two years. Without trying to stabilise the Swiss franc vis-a-vis the German mark, we have nevertheless been able to keep its fluctuations within acceptable margins. Our intention is to maintain such a flexible approach when the Monetary Union starts on 1.1.1999. 3. Conclusion In a few weeks, the historic step of introducing the European Monetary Union will create a new environment for monetary policy in Europe. The participating countries will be affected, but also the countries remaining outside. 8 In Switzerland, we see the appearance of the euro as a unique chance for Europe to promote monetary stability. A more stable monetary regime will be beneficial to everybody and will promote transparency and efficiency. We expect the Swiss franc to play a less important role as a transaction currency and the euro to be accepted as a means of payment within our country. Being a revolution, the introduction of the euro will be a source of uncertainty. But, as soon as the European Central Bank will be well established, we will have a good chance of seeing lower exchange rate volatility and lower interest rate differential between the franc and the euro. In the long run, given the strong correlation of economic fundamentals between Euroland and Switzerland, the foreign exchange market will consider the euro and the Swiss franc as two sister currencies.

Title: Monetary policy - The view from Switzerland
text: Monetary policy - Switzerland's point of view Hans Meyer Chairman of the Executive Board Swiss National Bank Belgian Financial Forum Brussels, 23 November 1998 2 1. The international economic situation You know the old adage that nothing is as permanent as change. Change is indeed one of the laws of existence. Experience shows that it is sometimes done quickly, sometimes more slowly. Currently, we are going through a phase of particularly intensive change. This intensity is mainly due to the accumulation of problems of various kinds and whose effects are, at least in appearance, negative. I am thinking in particular of the economic and social crises that have erupted in several regions of the world and of recent developments in the financial markets. The acute phase of transition we are experiencing requires differentiated judgment. In the medium to long term, the ongoing adaptation processes may prove to be entirely conducive to sustainable growth in the global economy. Experience teaches us, however, that transitions, even when they go in the right direction, can be critical moments. In both Western Europe and North America, developments are generally on the positive side. This is important as the economies in question still account for more than half of the global economy. The crisis that erupted more than a year ago in East Asia is still brewing. However, the affected countries are very dissimilar entities. The medium-sized states of South-East Asia, Indonesia, Korea and Japan cannot all be placed in one and the same category. With regard to the problems of this region, several observations, valid for the whole area, can nevertheless be made. Thus, unbalanced economic developments, fragile financial systems and insufficient supervision of financial markets are only symptoms of deeper causes. This also applies to a country such as Russia. Here, too, the problems are essentially social in nature. The country's economic weight and its links with the world economy are still relatively tenuous. But its size, 3 its potential wealth, and in particular its importance in terms of security policy, gives Russian events a special significance. Given its latent economic and political instability, Latin America is also a hotbed of potential crisis. Within this region, Brazil deserves special attention, since it represents economically speaking almost half of the area. As far as the global economy is concerned, the awakening has been brutal. The world's economic and social situation is clearly not balanced enough to ensure sustainable growth. Long-term adaptations, and probably also painful, have therefore become inevitable. In this regard, it is important that each country puts its own house in order. To accomplish this task, there is no need to resort to new recipes. The important thing is to resolutely and sustainably apply methods that have proven their worth. Any external aid, let us not forget, must be aimed exclusively at enabling the beneficiaries to take care of themselves. Emphasis on the responsibility of each State leads to a more realistic assessment of the opportunities and risks inherent in international economic relations. The division of labour at the international level, which derives from economic relations with foreign countries, is desirable and no one disputes that. But, here too, it must be remembered that the strength of a chain depends on its weakest link. Let us therefore make a more objective and, therefore, more realistic judgment on the opportunities and risks associated with this development! 2. Developments on the financial markets The problems that have arisen in the financial markets have not fallen from the sky. Thus, for some time now, the evolution of the securities markets has seemed to somehow evade objective analysis. The price gains recorded in the first months of the year then largely melted. 4 It will be recalled, however, in passing judgment on this development, that prices reached a very high level at the beginning of the year. The correction that has occurred seems likely to raise awareness that, while free and open markets offer opportunities, they also contain risks. If the opportunities and risks remain in reasonable proportions, this can be seen as a sign of the proper functioning of such markets. In this respect, however, it should be noted that transitions can be extremely difficult even if they go in the right direction. A rapid and sharp decline in stock prices can have a negative impact on the stability of the financial system and thus on the real economy. Viewed objectively, recent events do not, however, encourage us to speak of a critical development, at least as far as the markets of developed economies are concerned. Rather, it is an inevitable, and ultimately salutary, correction to developments in recent years. It will hopefully lead - to a more realistic assessment of things, which is essential for an efficient allocation of resources. For both economic and social reasons, it seems desirable that price fluctuations, which are normal and ultimately inevitable, should not exceed certain limits. Macroeconomically stable framework conditions and effective financial market surveillance can go a long way towards avoiding spillovers. Another observation seems important to me: slippages come much more often from contempt for elementary common sense than from a combination of complex facts. Common sense, modesty and solidity must help to restore things to more reasonable proportions. 5 3. The Swiss economic situation and monetary policy After a period of expansion in the second half of the eighties, the Swiss economy experienced an unusually long phase of stagnation in the first years of this decade. Since last year, there has been a recovery, more noticeable in my opinion in the evolution of the economic situation than in the actual extent of the recovery, on which we can in any case only speculate. Several factors contributed to this turnaround. I am thinking above all of the monetary framework conditions, the structural changes that have been taking place for some time and the economic recovery in our main foreign partners. In the future too, the development of the Swiss economy will remain highly dependent on developments abroad. Unless unforeseen, real growth of about 2% can be expected for the current year and about 1.5% for 1999. This pace corresponds approximately to the medium-term growth potential of our economy. In addition, our price level is stable and unemployment is declining happily. However, efforts will be needed to ensure a continued recovery. In this respect, economic agents are called upon to play a decisive role. To do this, they must benefit from framework conditions favourable to their activities and therefore conducive to sustainable growth. Let us not forget that it is precisely they, this time as citizens, who must create these framework conditions! The establishment of favourable framework conditions, and this is an essential point, is an ongoing challenge. In this respect, it is both false and harmful to imagine that there are simple, quick and ready-made solutions. Indeed, this is a long-term task, which must be carried out with determination and perseverance, particularly in the areas of budgetary policy, competition policy and monetary policy. 6 The Swiss National Bank's mission is to conduct a monetary policy that serves the general interests of the country. In concrete terms, it must participate, taking into account the possibilities of monetary policy, in creating conditions for balanced and, therefore, sustainable growth of the national economy. In our view, the best contribution that monetary policy can make is to ensure the stability of the price level, i.e. to keep the rate of inflation between 1% and 2%. It follows from the above that price level stability is not an end in itself, but only a means to achieve the objective. In recent decades, economics has convincingly demonstrated that the lack of price level stability can lead to significant losses in growth and prosperity. In addition, rising prices penalize above all the economically weak sections of the population. Price stability is therefore an eminently social priority. Since its foundation at the beginning of this century, the SNB has been autonomous and conducts monetary policy within the framework of its mandate. The independence enjoyed by an institution governed by public law cannot be absolute in a democratic society. By virtue of its supervisory powers under the law, the Federal Government has the right and the obligation to ensure that the SNB fulfils its mandate in an appropriate manner, i.e. on the basis of the lessons of economic science and experience. The conduct of an appropriate monetary policy is a challenge that concerns not only the economy, but also and above all society as a whole. The establishment of institutional conditions and their long-term observance presuppose a broad consensus within society on the fundamental issues, in other words on the importance of a policy of lasting stability. The central bank must earn confidence through the medium-term success of its policy. By carrying out its actions in a transparent manner, it promotes the formation of such a consensus. 7 In the conduct of monetary policy itself, the central bank must rely on the obvious link which, as economic theory and experience demonstrate, exists tendentially and in the medium term between the supply of money to the economy and the stability of the price level. Finally, it is therefore necessary to adapt, to an appropriate extent, the supply of money to real economic developments. Monetary impulses, experience shows, are reflected in prices and output only after a fairly long and variable period of time. For this reason, central banks have always used monetary aggregates as indicators or intermediate monetary objectives to conduct their policies. Monetary aggregates lend themselves well to the role of intermediate objectives when they can be easily managed and, moreover, there is a close correlation between them and the ultimate objective of monetary policy, namely price level stability. In the recent period, these conditions have been less and less met in several countries, given developments in the financial markets. Another strategy, which focuses directly on an inflation target, has therefore received more attention. Since the switch to floating exchange rates, the Swiss National Bank has been pragmatically pursuing a policy of managing a monetary aggregate. Overall, we have had good experiences with this strategy. In recent times, however, shifts in demand for central money have given us a hard time. We, too, are therefore called upon to examine whether the strategy based on an inflation target can offer an alternative to our policy of managing a monetary aggregate. A central bank that has opted for the inflation target strategy seeks to achieve price level stability directly, i.e. it operates without recourse to an intermediate target. It must therefore make a prognosis for the evolution of inflation and, according to it, decide on its monetary policy so that its prognosis and the inflation target overlap. Proponents of this approach believe that monetary policy thus becomes more transparent for 8 market operators. However, if the objective is not achieved, it is not easy to determine the causes and thus the responsibilities. In practice, the implementation of an inflation-oriented monetary policy is generally more difficult, due to the difficulty of making reliable forecasts of the evolution of inflation in the short and medium term. This objection is particularly relevant in the case of a small economy that is very open to foreign countries. Indeed, the evolution of the increase in prices depends strongly on developments observed abroad. In addition, it is difficult to accurately assess the variation that short-term interest rates need to be given to achieve the inflation target. Here, economics reaches the limits of its possibilities. Our strategy, as I have already pointed out, is based on the management of a monetary aggregate, but we are pragmatic in its implementation. We therefore believe that it is ultimately no different from that based on an inflation target. We set our objective in terms of a monetary aggregate so as to achieve price level stability according to the definition I have just given. It is therefore a conditional objective. In addition, our goal is set for the medium term, i.e. for several years. Thus, we can, if the situation so requires, temporarily deviate from the growth path set for the monetary aggregate. One of the advantages of this strategy is that setting the target in terms of a monetary aggregate creates an operational framework for monetary policy. We believe that this promotes transparency. In our view, a change in strategy - the move towards an inflation target - is only conceivable if the correlation between the development of the money supply and that of the price level were to be permanently disturbed. As you know, the European Central Bank has recently taken a position on the strategy it intends to adopt for its monetary policy. On this occasion, it defined its conception of price stability. It also announced its intention not to set an inflation target and to attribute an important role to the evolution of the 9 monetary aggregates. I am therefore pleased to note that we largely share the same ideas. 4. European Monetary Union At the beginning of next year, European monetary union will become a reality. Important countries on our continent will give a new framework to their monetary relations, in the context of the process of European integration. Even if monetary union is not essential, it offers a sensible complement to the single market. Institutionally, the creation of a European Central Bank and the issuance of a single currency, the euro, are key elements. In substance, it is important that the European Central Bank be independent of governments and that its primary objective is price level stability. Its policy, it has been expected, will be supported by a fiscal policy focused on stability in the countries participating in the Monetary Union. If these ideas come to fruition, the framework conditions for favourable economic development will improve significantly in Europe. Given the close economic ties between Switzerland and the European single market, we have every interest in such a development. Balanced cross-border economic developments imply stable monetary relations, and therefore a policy of stability that converges sustainably in the main countries concerned. This is a challenge that concerns not only the economy, but also society as a whole. Will the participants in monetary union be willing and able to commit themselves to the discipline necessary for such a policy on a lasting basis? This is a crucial issue. For efforts to be sustainable, institutional capacity is not enough. It is indeed necessary for the policy of stability to be a condition for development. 10 prosperous economy, is the subject of a broad consensus. Such a consensus must be reflected in the concrete actions of the people, parliament and government. The establishment of fixed exchange rate relations implies the loss of an element of flexibility for the economic policies of the countries concerned, which may raise a problem since, already today, the capacity to adapt is insufficient. Given the foreseeable need for adaptation, the problem is particularly acute, especially if flexibility is lacking in labour markets. A shortfall in this area would lead to an increase in unemployment. Basically, a small country like Switzerland has two options to choose from when it comes to its cross-border monetary relations. It can renounce an autonomous policy by tying its currency to that of another country, which in reality forces it to resume the monetary policy conducted by that country. The other possibility is to opt for an exchange rate regime offering flexible monetary relations and thus to allow oneself a certain autonomy. There is no such thing as an ideal solution. The link to the currency of another country may be considered if the policy pursued by the partner corresponds to the ideas of the small country and if, moreover, the latter can count on the fact that, in all probability, nothing will change in this respect. The second condition is almost never met, which argues in favour of the solution offering greater room for manoeuvre. In the coming years, it will be a question of keeping our own house in order, or even putting it back in order. In this way, we will make the best possible contribution, including to international solidarity. We will also have to maintain our traditional openness to the outside world. Relations with our neighbours, close and not so close, will have to be rethought taking into account the evolution of our environment. This will require, first and foremost, that the conditions be created internally. If monetary union is achieved in Europe as planned, the euro will tend to be a stable currency. It will then have the chance to gradually become one of the world's leading currencies. With a stable euro, the Swiss franc will have no negative repercussions to fear. If, however, monetary union were to be 11 Built in haste, in defiance of economic conditions, turbulence should be expected. In this case, the Swiss franc could come under upward pressure. Basically, the SNB would then have the opportunity to counter the trend towards the revaluation of the Swiss franc by easing its monetary policy. But such a strategy, we must be well aware, could conflict with our stability-oriented policy. 5. Summary Let me summarize my thinking as follows. The global economy is currently going through a phase of transition. Drifts must be corrected. But, and this seems to me to be even more important, we must also draw lessons from it that will be invaluable to us in the search for balanced and sustainable economic growth. I would like to recall three thoughts: Let us not strive to reinvent the wheel, but rather to ensure that the objectives of the economy and society as a whole are better compatible with human and material realities. Common sense, diligence and a certain modesty must guide the way forward. - The international division of labour is an idea in itself attractive. For it to work successfully, it is essential that each country meets the required conditions. Only links between healthy economies can lead to the expected benefits. The characteristics of an appropriate economic policy are the same for all. Above all, we need a stability-oriented monetary policy, a sound fiscal policy and an effective competition policy. Aid from the strong to the weakest serves the interests of all. However, it is only really profitable if it is designed to allow beneficiaries to get by on their own. - Finally, let us never forget that creating the conditions conducive to balanced and sustainable economic growth is ultimately a challenge that concerns 12 society as a whole. It is indeed men who decide on the framework conditions under which they carry out their economic activities. The challenge is overcome only if a sufficient number of citizens take an active part in shaping the conditions of life in society.

Je songe notamment aux crises conomiques et sociales qui ont clat dans plusieurs rgions du globe ainsi qu'aux dveloppements rcents sur les marchs financiers. La phase aigu de transition que nous vivons ncessite un jugement diffrenci. A moyen ou long terme, les processus d'adaptation en cours peuvent s'avrer tout  fait propices  une croissance durable de l'conomie mondiale. L'exprience nous enseigne cependant que les transitions, mme lorsqu'elles vont dans la bonne direction, peuvent constituer des moments critiques. Tant en Europe occidentale qu'en Amrique du Nord, l'volution suit dans l'ensemble un cours positif. Cette constatation est importante dans la mesure o les conomies en question reprsentent aujourd'hui encore plus de la moiti de l'conomie mondiale. La crise qui a clat il y a plus d'un an dj en Asie de l'Est couve toujours. Or, les pays touchs constituent des entits fort dissemblables. Les Etats de taille moyenne du Sud-Est asiatique, l'Indonsie, la Core et le Japon ne sauraient en effet tre rangs tous dans une seule et mme catgorie. En ce qui concerne les problmes de cette rgion, plusieurs constatations, valables pour l'ensemble de la zone, peuvent nanmoins tre formules. Ainsi, une volution conomique dsquilibre, des systmes financiers fragiles et une surveillance insuffisante des marchs financiers ne sont-ils que des symptmes de causes plus profondes. Ce constat s'applique galement  un pays tel que la Russie. Ici aussi, les problmes sont de nature essentiellement sociale. Le poids conomique du pays et ses liens avec l'conomie mondiale sont encore relativement tnus. Mais sa taille, 3 sa richesse potentielle et notamment son importance sur le plan de la politique de scurit confrent aux vnements russes une porte particulire. Vu son instabilit conomique et politique latente, l'Amrique latine est elle aussi un foyer de crise potentiel. Au sein de cette rgion, le Brsil mrite une attention particulire, puisqu'il reprsente conomiquement parlant prs de la moiti de la zone. Pour ce qui a trait  l'conomie mondiale, le rveil a t brutal. La situation conomique et sociale du monde n'est manifestement pas assez quilibre pour garantir une croissance durable. Des adaptations de longue haleine, et sans doute aussi douloureuses, sont par consquent devenues inluctables. A ce propos, il importe que chaque pays mette de l'ordre dans sa propre maison. Pour remplir cette tche, point n'est besoin de recourir  de nouvelles recettes. L'important est d'appliquer rsolument et durablement des mthodes qui ont fait leurs preuves. Toute aide extrieure, ne l'oublions pas, doit viser exclusivement  permettre aux bnficiaires de se prendre en charge eux-mmes. En mettant l'accent sur la responsabilit de chaque Etat, on aboutit  une apprciation plus raliste des chances et des risques inhrents aux relations conomiques internationales. La division du travail sur le plan international, qui dcoule des relations conomiques avec l'tranger, est souhaitable et personne ne le conteste. Mais, ici aussi, il faut se souvenir que la solidit d'une chane dpend de son maillon le plus faible. Portons donc un jugement plus objectif et, par consquent, plus raliste sur les chances et les risques lis  cette volution! 2. L'volution sur les marchs financiers Les problmes qui ont surgi sur les marchs financiers ne sont pas tombs du ciel. Ainsi, depuis un certain temps, l'volution des marchs des valeurs mobilires a sembl en quelque sorte se drober  une analyse objective. Les gains de cours enregistrs dans les premiers mois de l'anne ont ensuite fondu en grande partie. 4 On se rappellera pourtant, en portant un jugement sur cette volution, que les cours atteignaient un niveau trs lev au dbut de l'anne. La correction qui s'est produite parat de nature  faire mieux prendre conscience que, si des marchs libres et ouverts offrent des chances, ils reclent aussi des risques. Si les chances et les risques se maintiennent dans des proportions raisonnables, on peut y voir un signe de bon fonctionnement de tels marchs. A cet gard, il faut toutefois relever que des transitions peuvent s'avrer extrmement difficiles mme si elles vont dans la bonne direction. Une baisse  la fois rapide et forte des cours des actions peut avoir des consquences nfastes sur la stabilit du systme financier et, partant, sur l'conomie relle. Considrs avec objectivit, les vnements rcents n'incitent cependant pas  parler d'une volution critique, en tout cas pour ce qui concerne les marchs des conomies dveloppes. Il s'agit plutt d'une correction inluctable, et en fin de compte salutaire, de l'volution observe ces dernires annes. Elle conduira esprons-le -  une apprciation plus raliste des choses, ce qui est essentiel pour une allocation efficiente des ressources. Pour des raisons tant conomiques que sociales, il semble souhaitable que les fluctuations des cours, qui sont normales et finalement inluctables, n'excdent pas certaines limites. Des conditions-cadres stables sur le plan macroconomique et une surveillance efficace des marchs financiers sont de nature  contribuer grandement  viter des dbordements. Une autre constatation me parat importante: les drapages proviennent bien plus souvent du mpris du bon sens lmentaire que d'une conjonction de faits complexes. Le bon sens, la modestie et la solidit doivent contribuer  ce que les choses retrouvent des proportions plus raisonnables. 5 3. La situation conomique et la politique montaire suisses Aprs une priode d'expansion dans la seconde moiti des annes quatre-vingt, l'conomie suisse a connu, au cours des premires annes de la prsente dcennie, une phase de stagnation inhabituellement longue. Depuis l'an dernier, on observe un redmarrage, plus perceptible  mon avis dans l'volution de la conjoncture que dans l'ampleur effective de la reprise, sur laquelle on ne peut de toute manire que spculer. Plusieurs facteurs ont contribu  ce revirement. Je pense avant tout aux conditions-cadres sur le plan montaire, aux mutations structurelles que l'on enregistre depuis un certain temps et  la reprise conomique chez nos principaux partenaires trangers. A l'avenir galement, l'volution de l'conomie suisse restera fortement dpendante de l'volution  l'tranger. Sauf imprvu, on peut tabler sur une croissance relle d'environ 2% pour l'anne en cours et de 1,5% environ pour 1999. Ce rythme correspond approximativement au potentiel de croissance  moyen terme de notre conomie. En outre, notre niveau des prix est stable et le chmage enregistre un repli rjouissant. Des efforts seront toutefois indispensables si l'on veut garantir la poursuite de la reprise. En la matire, les agents conomiques sont appels  jouer un rle dcisif. Pour cela, ils doivent bnficier de conditions-cadres favorables  leurs activits et partant propices  une croissance durable. Or, n'oublions pas que ce sont prcisment eux, en leur qualit de citoyens cette fois, qui doivent crer ces conditions-cadres! La mise en place de conditions-cadres favorables, et c'est l un point essentiel, constitue un dfi permanent. A cet gard, il est  la fois faux et nuisible de s'imaginer qu'il existe des solutions simples, rapides et toutes faites. En effet, il s'agit d'un travail de longue haleine, qui doit tre men avec dtermination et persvrance, notamment dans les domaines de la politique budgtaire, de la politique de la concurrence et de la politique montaire. 6 La Banque nationale suisse a pour mission de mener une politique montaire servant les intrts gnraux du pays. Concrtement, elle doit participer, compte tenu des possibilits de la politique montaire,  la mise en place de conditions permettant une croissance quilibre et, partant, durable de l'conomie nationale. A notre avis, la meilleure contribution que la politique montaire puisse fournir consiste  garantir la stabilit du niveau des prix, soit  maintenir le taux de renchrissement entre 1% et 2%. Il ressort de ce qui prcde que la stabilit du niveau des prix n'est pas une fin en soi, mais uniquement un moyen permettant d'atteindre l'objectif. Au cours des dernires dcennies, la science conomique a dmontr de manire convaincante que l'absence de stabilit du niveau des prix peut conduire  d'importantes pertes de croissance et de prosprit. De plus, le renchrissement pnalise avant tout les couches conomiquement faibles de la population. La stabilit des prix est donc une priorit de porte minemment sociale. Depuis sa fondation au dbut de ce sicle, la Banque nationale est autonome et conduit la politique montaire dans le cadre du mandat qui lui est assign. Or, l'indpendance dont jouit une institution de droit public ne saurait tre absolue dans une socit dmocratique. En vertu des attributions que la loi lui confre en matire de surveillance, le Gouvernement fdral a en effet le droit et l'obligation de veiller  ce que la Banque nationale remplisse son mandat de manire approprie, soit en se fondant sur les enseignements de la science conomique et des expriences faites. La conduite d'une politique montaire approprie est un dfi qui concerne non seulement l'conomie, mais aussi et surtout la socit dans son ensemble. La mise en place de conditions institutionnelles et leur respect dans la dure prsupposent un large consensus, au sein de la socit, sur les enjeux fondamentaux, en d'autres termes sur l'importance que revt une politique de stabilit durable. La banque centrale doit mriter la confiance par le succs,  moyen terme, de sa politique. En menant ses actions de manire transparente, elle favorise la formation d'un tel consensus. 7 Pour la conduite de la politique montaire  proprement parler, la banque centrale doit se fonder sur le lien vident qui, comme le dmontrent la thorie conomique et l'exprience, existe tendanciellement et  moyen terme entre l'approvisionnement de l'conomie en monnaie et la stabilit du niveau des prix. Finalement, il s'agit donc d'adapter, dans une mesure approprie, l'approvisionnement en monnaie  l'volution conomique relle. Les impulsions montaires, l'exprience le montre, ne se rpercutent sur les prix et la production qu'aprs un laps de temps assez long et variable. C'est pourquoi les banques centrales ont toujours recouru, pour conduire leur politique,  des agrgats montaires en tant qu'indicateurs ou en tant qu'objectifs montaires intermdiaires. Les agrgats montaires se prtent bien au rle d'objectifs intermdiaires lorsqu'ils peuvent tre grs aisment et que, de plus, une corrlation troite existe entre eux et l'objectif ultime de la politique montaire,  savoir la stabilit du niveau des prix. Dans la priode rcente, ces conditions ont t de moins en moins remplies, dans plusieurs pays, compte tenu des volutions sur les marchs financiers. Une autre stratgie, qui est axe directement sur un objectif d'inflation, a par consquent davantage retenu l'attention. Depuis le passage aux changes flottants, la Banque nationale suisse mne de faon pragmatique une politique de gestion d'un agrgat montaire. Dans l'ensemble, nous avons fait de bonnes expriences avec cette stratgie. Ces derniers temps, des dplacements de la demande de monnaie centrale nous ont toutefois donn du fil  retordre. Nous sommes donc, nous aussi, amens  examiner si la stratgie reposant sur un objectif d'inflation peut offrir une solution de rechange  notre politique de gestion d'un agrgat montaire. Une banque centrale ayant opt pour la stratgie reposant sur un objectif d'inflation cherche  atteindre directement la stabilit du niveau des prix, c'est--dire qu'elle opre sans recourir  un objectif intermdiaire. Elle doit donc tablir un pronostic pour l'volution de l'inflation et, en fonction de celui-ci, arrter sa politique montaire pour que son pronostic et l'objectif d'inflation se recoupent. Les partisans de cette approche estiment que la politique montaire devient ainsi plus transparente pour 8 les oprateurs sur les marchs. Cependant, si l'objectif n'est pas atteint, il n'est gure ais d'en dterminer les causes et, partant, les responsabilits. En pratique, la mise en  uvre d'une politique montaire axe sur un objectif d'inflation est gnralement plus ardue, du fait de la difficult  tablir des prvisions fiables quant  l'volution de l'inflation  court et moyen termes. Cette objection est particulirement pertinente dans le cas d'une petite conomie trs ouverte sur l'tranger. En effet, l'volution du renchrissement dpend fortement des dveloppements observs  l'tranger. De plus, il est difficile d'valuer avec prcision la variation  donner aux taux d'intrt  court terme pour atteindre l'objectif d'inflation. Ici, la science conomique atteint les limites de ses possibilits. Notre stratgie, je l'ai dj soulign, est axe sur la gestion d'un agrgat montaire, mais nous faisons preuve de pragmatisme dans sa mise en  uvre. Nous estimons par consquent qu'elle ne diffre en dfinitive gure de celle qui repose sur un objectif d'inflation. Nous fixons notre objectif en termes d'un agrgat montaire de faon  atteindre la stabilit du niveau des prix selon la dfinition que je viens d'en donner. Il s'agit par consquent d'un objectif conditionnel. De plus, notre objectif est arrt pour le moyen terme, soit pour plusieurs annes. Ainsi, nous pouvons, si la situation l'exige, nous carter temporairement du sentier de croissance fix pour l'agrgat montaire. L'un des avantages de cette stratgie rside dans le fait que la dtermination de l'objectif en termes d'un agrgat montaire cre un cadre oprationnel pour la politique montaire. Nous estimons que cela favorise la transparence. Un changement de stratgie - le passage  un objectif d'inflation - n'est  notre avis envisageable que si la corrlation entre l'vo-lution de la masse montaire et celle du niveau des prix devait tre durablement perturbe. La Banque centrale europenne, vous le savez, a pris rcemment position sur la stratgie qu'elle entend adopter pour sa politique montaire. A cette occasion, elle a dfini sa conception de la stabilit des prix. Elle a aussi annonc son intention de ne pas fixer un objectif d'inflation et d'attribuer un rle important  l'volution des 9 agrgats montaires. Je constate donc avec satisfaction que nous partageons largement les mmes ides. 4. L'Union montaire europenne Au dbut de l'anne prochaine, l'Union montaire europenne deviendra ralit. D'importants pays de notre continent donneront un cadre nouveau  leurs relations montaires, dans le contexte du processus d'intgration europenne. Quand bien mme l'Union montaire n'est pas indispensable, elle offre un complment judicieux au march unique. Sur le plan institutionnel, la cration d'une Banque centrale europenne et l'mission d'une monnaie unique, l'euro, sont des lments cls. Sur le fond, il est important que la Banque centrale europenne soit indpendante des gouvernements et qu'elle ait avant tout pour objectif la stabilit du niveau des prix. Sa politique, a-t-on prvu, sera soutenue par une politique budgtaire axe sur la stabilit dans les pays participant  l'Union montaire. Si ces ides se concrtisent, les conditions-cadres pour une volution conomique favorable s'amlioreront sensiblement en Europe. Etant donn les liens conomiques troits entre la Suisse et le march unique europen, nous avons tout intrt  une telle volution. Une volution conomique transfrontire quilibre implique des relations montaires stables, donc une politique de stabilit qui converge durablement dans les principaux pays concerns. C'est l un dfi qui concerne non seulement l'conomie, mais aussi la socit dans son ensemble. Les participants  l'Union montaire auront-ils la volont et seront-ils en mesure de s'astreindre durablement  la discipline indispensable  une telle politique? Cette question est cruciale. Pour que les efforts soient durables, les moyens institutionnels ne suffisent pas. Il est en effet ncessaire que la politique de stabilit, condition d'une volution 10 conomique prospre, fasse l'objet d'un large consensus. Un tel consensus doit se rpercuter dans les actes concrets du peuple, du parlement et du gouvernement. L'tablissement de relations de change fixes implique, pour la politique conomique des pays concerns, la perte d'un lment de souplesse, ce qui peut soulever un problme dans la mesure o, aujourd'hui dj, la capacit d'adaptation est insuffisante. Compte tenu du besoin prvisible d'adaptation, le problme revt une acuit toute particulire, surtout si la souplesse fait dfaut sur les marchs du travail. Une insuffisance dans ce domaine se traduirait par une aggravation du chmage. Fondamentalement, un petit pays comme la Suisse a le choix entre deux possibilits en ce qui concerne ses relations montaires transfrontires. Il peut renoncer  une politique autonome en liant sa monnaie  celle d'un autre pays, ce qui le contraint en ralit  reprendre la politique montaire mene par ce pays. L'autre possibilit consiste  opter pour un rgime de change offrant des relations montaires souples et, ainsi,  se mnager une certaine autonomie. La solution idale n'existe pas. Le lien  la monnaie d'un autre pays peut tre envisag si la politique mene par le partenaire correspond aux ides du petit pays et si, de surcrot, ce dernier peut tabler sur le fait que, selon toute probabilit, rien ne changera  cet gard. La seconde condition n'est pour ainsi dire jamais remplie, ce qui plaide en faveur de la solution offrant une plus grande marge de manoeuvre. Ces prochaines annes, il s'agira pour nous de maintenir notre propre maison en ordre, voire d'y remettre de l'ordre. Nous apporterons ainsi la meilleure des contributions possibles, y compris  la solidarit sur le plan international. Nous devrons galement conserver notre ouverture traditionnelle sur l'tranger. Les relations avec nos voisins, proches et moins proches, devront tre repenses en tenant compte de l'volution de notre environnement. Pour cela, il faudra d'abord et avant tout que les conditions soient cres sur le plan interne. Si l'Union montaire se ralise en Europe comme prvu, l'euro aura plutt tendance  tre une monnaie stable. Il aura alors la chance de devenir progressivement l'une des principales monnaies mondiales. Avec un euro stable, le franc suisse n'aura aucune rpercussion ngative  craindre. Si l'Union montaire devait toutefois tre 11 btie dans la prcipitation, au mpris des conditions indispensables sur le plan conomique, il faudrait s'attendre  des turbulences. Dans ce cas, le franc suisse risquerait de subir des pressions  la hausse. Fondamentalement, la Banque nationale aurait alors la possibilit de contrer, par un assouplissement de sa politique montaire, la tendance  la revalorisation du franc. Mais une telle stratgie, il faut en tre bien conscient, pourrait entrer en conflit avec notre politique axe sur la stabilit. 5. Rsum Permettez-moi de rsumer ma pense comme il suit. L'conomie mondiale traverse actuellement une phase de transition. Des drives doivent tre corriges. Mais, et cela me parat plus important encore, il nous faut aussi en tirer des enseignements qui nous seront prcieux dans la recherche d'une croissance conomique quilibre et durable. Je voudrais rappeler trois rflexions: - Efforons-nous non pas de rinventer la roue, mais bien plutt de faire en sorte que les objectifs de l'conomie et de la socit dans son ensemble soient mieux compatibles avec les ralits humaines et matrielles. Le bon sens, la diligence et une certaine modestie doivent baliser la voie  suivre. - La division internationale du travail est une ide en soi sduisante. Pour qu'elle fonctionne avec succs, il est essentiel que chaque pays remplisse les conditions requises. Seuls des liens tisss entre des conomies saines peuvent conduire aux avantages esprs. Les caractristiques d'une politique conomique approprie sont les mmes pour tous. Il faut avant tout une politique montaire axe sur la stabilit, une politique budgtaire solide et une politique de la concurrence efficace. L'aide des forts aux plus faibles sert les intrts de tous. Cependant, elle n'est vraiment profitable que si elle est conue pour permettre aux bnficiaires de s'en sortir par eux-mmes. - Enfin, n'oublions jamais que la mise en place de conditions propices  une croissance conomique quilibre et durable est finalement un dfi qui concerne 12 la socit dans son ensemble. Ce sont en effet les hommes qui dcident des conditions-cadres dans lesquelles ils exercent leurs activits conomiques. Le dfi n'est surmont que si un nombre suffisant de citoyennes et de citoyens prennent une part active  l'amnagement des conditions de la vie en socit.

Title: Introductory Remarks, End-of-year Media News Conference, Zrich
text: Year-end press conference, Zurich, 11 December 1998 Introductory remarks by Bruno Gehrig, Member of the Governing Board of the Swiss National Bank Lessons to be learned from financial market turbulence A look at the last few weeks shows first of all that the situation has calmed down markedly on the financial markets, after a tumultuous phase, in October above all. That finding cannot exempt operators on the markets from carrying out a critical analysis of the experiences gained and from drawing lessons from them. Such an exercise seems to me all the more necessary since most observers have allowed themselves to be surprised, on two levels especially, by the course of events. A first surprise came from the intensity and extent of the chain reactions between markets, especially after Russia's unilaterally decreed moratorium on its debt. That such a shock could have had repercussions not only on the markets of emerging economies, but also on the corporate bond market in the United States is a new development. This shows that reactions to a shock, with modern methods of portfolio management, are not limited to certain markets, but extend to the entire portfolio. Therefore, while diversification can reduce risk  a reduction that can be expected under normal circumstances  it can also lose such benefits in high-tension situations. A second surprise stemmed from the sharp erosion of market liquidity, which was observed even in the well-developed US government securities market. Many investment funds and securities houses suddenly all found themselves on the selling side, resulting in limited tradingability, and unexpectedly, even for normally very liquid positions. Many remained stuck with positions that, from a risk point of view, were undesirable, even dangerous. Lessons should be learned from these experiences, above all from the exceptional case where operators are all surprised in the same way and, therefore, all want to react in the same direction. The risks that an actor is willing to bear must also include situations of greater tension and, in view of the events that can arise during crises, more diversified. In this regard, particular account must be taken of the fact that shocks can deprive the market of its liquidity. Actors are then faced with a dilemma: it is precisely in a phase that urgently calls for portfolio adaptations that the margin available to react suddenly becomes very narrow. In their own interest, market participants would do well to swiftly and rigorously implement their findings. This will lead, in most cases, to a reduction in tolerated value at risk and leverage. Knowing how to keep the right proportions is the essential condition for the free movement of capital to be economically relevant over time. Money market management under more difficult conditions The uncertainty that has characterized the financial markets and prompted traders to turn more to "safe" currencies has led to a trend towards the revaluation of the franc. To counter this trend that could put our economic recovery at risk, we have generously supplied the market with liquidity; interest rates below the discount rate were thus applied for several days. In the management of the money market, we also had to take into account exceptional movements in the demand for credit transfer accounts. The propensity to take less counterparty risk  an effect of market uncertainty  has led several banks to temporarily hold a precautionary cash balance in the form of transfer account holdings. These assets have thus reached some days levels above 5 billion francs. Such levels give a grossly exaggerated impression of the expansionary nature of monetary policy. The increased use of repo in interbank transactions will reduce these disruptions in demand for central money. Indeed, the characteristic of repurchase agreements is precisely to minimize counterparty risk. They therefore offer an attractive alternative to a stronger holding of assets in unpaid transfer accounts at the SNB. Contribution to the internationalisation of the financial centre's infrastructure Cross-border integration of financial markets is already under way. The changeover to the euro will further accentuate the concentration movement in the areas of stock exchanges and securities management. As a central bank, we have a vested interest in ensuring that increasingly integrated markets have well-adapted infrastructure for the settlement of transactions. The future belongs to cross-border settlement systems which, in terms of safety and efficiency, meet standards as high as those of national systems. Only in this way will systemic risks be controlled. Efficient settlement systems are also a prerequisite for achieving fair competition between financial centres. Efforts to increase the efficiency of settlement systems are under way globally. The TARGET (Trans-european Automated Real-time Gross settlement Express Transfer) system, which will handle payments in euros, will soon enter into operation in the EU. The Swiss banks will jointly operate an institution (the "Swiss EURO Clearing Bank", SECB) which will operate in Frankfurt am Main, with SIC technology, and thus indirectly connect them to TARGET. For its euro operations, the SNB will also use the services of ECBC. By opening up the SIC to foreign clearing bodies and to major players operating abroad on the markets, the SNB can contribute to the development of more reliable settlement infrastructures. It supports the CLS ("Continuous Linked Settlement") project of the major commercial banks. This ambitious project aims to eliminate settlement risks in foreign exchange transactions. The SNB is keenly interested in establishing an efficient connection with the SIC, the Swiss franc payment system. The criteria for access to the CIS have been adapted to take account of such developments. Joint ventures and clearing bodies operating internationally (CLS in particular), as well as the participating banks, can in principle access the SIC remotely, provided that this results in a reduction in systemic risks or a strengthening of the Swiss financial centre. The beneficiaries of this remote access must also be subject to rules on banking supervision and the fight against money laundering that are at least as strict as those in force in Switzerland. Remote access is already being carried out for the German members of EUREX, the derivatives exchange. It is also open to members of the Swiss Stock Exchange who operate from abroad. Finally, remote access to the SIC will be open to foreign players in the Swiss franc repo market from spring 1999, when the "Repo International" stage will be completed. To be accepted, however, the participant must meet, on the ticket side, the requirements required by the "delivery against payment" principle. He will therefore have to open a deposit at SEGA, the Swiss Company for the transfer of SA securities. Thanks to this infrastructure, it will be possible to switch monetary policy operations with counterparties abroad. With this in mind, government bonds, denominated in major foreign currencies, will also be included in the basket of securities that the SNB has defined for its repo operations. The basket will be expanded as soon as an effective "delivery against payment" payment payment payment is ensured. Is there not a risk that the SNB will lose control of the money market after the opening of the SIC? This fear is not justified. The assets in transfer accounts will remain fully transparent for us. In addition, foreign participants will have few assets in transfer accounts at the end of the day, as they do not have to meet liquidity arrangements in Swiss francs. We are convinced that these two openings  more counterparties and more repurchase agreements  are likely to strengthen the Swiss franc money market and make the implementation of monetary policy more efficient.
text_original: Confrence de presse de fin d'anne, Zurich, 11 dcembre 1998 Remarques introductives de Bruno Gehrig, Membre de la Direction gnrale de la Banque nationale suisse Les leons  tirer des turbulences sur les marchs financiers Un regard sur ces dernires semaines permet de constater d'abord que la situation s'est nettement apaise sur les marchs financiers, aprs une phase tumultueuse, en octobre avant tout. Cette constatation ne saurait dispenser les oprateurs sur les marchs de procder  une analyse critique des expriences faites et d'en tirer des enseignements. Un tel exercice me parat d'autant plus ncessaire que la plupart des observateurs se sont laiss surprendre, sur deux plans surtout, par le cours des vnements. Une premire surprise est venue de l'intensit et de l'tendue des ractions en chane entre les marchs, en particulier aprs le moratoire dcrt unilatralement par la Russie sur sa dette. Qu'un tel choc ait pu avoir des rpercussions non seulement sur les marchs des conomies mergentes, mais aussi sur le march des obligations des entreprises industrielles aux Etats-Unis constitue un fait nouveau. Cela montre que les ractions  un choc, avec les mthodes modernes de gestion de portefeuille, ne se limitent pas  certains marchs, mais s'tendent  l'ensemble du portefeuille. Par consquent, si la diversification peut rduire les risques  rduction sur laquelle il est possible de compter dans des circonstances normales , elle peut aussi perdre de tels avantages dans des situations de vives tensions. Beaucoup sont rests bloqus avec des positions qui, du point de vue des risques, taient indsirables, voire dangereuses. Il convient de tirer des leons de ces expriences, avant tout du cas exceptionnel o les oprateurs sont tous surpris de manire identique et, par consquent, veulent tous ragir dans le mme sens. Les risques qu'un acteur est prt  supporter doivent inclure aussi des situations de tensions plus pousses et, eu gard aux pripties qui peuvent surgir lors de crises, plus diversifies. Il faut  ce propos tenir compte en particulier du fait que des chocs peuvent priver le march de sa liquidit. Les acteurs sont alors placs face  un dilemme: c'est prcisment dans une phase qui appelle de toute urgence des adaptations de portefeuille que la marge  disposition pour ragir devient soudain trs troite. Dans leur propre intrt, les acteurs sur les marchs feraient bien d'appliquer rapidement et rigoureusement leurs conclusions. Cela aboutira, dans la plupart des cas,  une rduction de la "value at risk" tolre et des effets de levier. Savoir garder de justes proportions est la condition indispensable  remplir pour que la libre circulation des capitaux soit conomiquement pertinente dans le temps. Gestion du march montaire dans des conditions plus ardues L'incertitude qui a caractris les marchs financiers et incit les oprateurs  se tourner davantage vers les monnaies "sres" a engendr une tendance  la revalorisation du franc. Pour contrer cette tendance de nature  mettre notre reprise conomique en danger, nous avons approvisionn gnreusement le march en liquidits; des taux d'intrt infrieurs au taux de l'escompte ont t ainsi appliqus pendant plusieurs jours. Dans la gestion du march montaire, nous avons d tenir compte galement de mouvements exceptionnels de la demande d'avoirs en comptes de virements. La propension  prendre moins de risques de contrepartie  un effet de l'incertitude rgnant sur les marchs  a amen plusieurs banques  dtenir temporairement une encaisse de prcaution sous forme d'avoirs en comptes de virements. Ces avoirs ont ainsi atteint certains jours des niveaux suprieurs  5 milliards de francs. De tels niveaux donnent une impression nettement exagre du caractre expansionniste de la politique montaire. Le recours accru aux pensions de titres dans les oprations interbancaires permettra de rduire ces perturbations dans la demande de monnaie centrale. En effet, les pensions de titres ont prcisment pour caractristique de minimiser le risque de contrepartie. Elles offrent par consquent une solution de rechange attrayante  une dtention plus forte d'avoirs en comptes de virements non rmunrs  la Banque nationale. Contribution  l'internationalisation des infrastructures de la place financire L'intgration transfrontire des marchs financiers est dj pousse. Le passage  l'euro accentuera encore le mouvement de concentration dans les domaines des Bourses et de la gestion de titres. En tant que banque centrale, nous avons tout intrt  ce que des marchs de plus en plus intgrs disposent d'infrastructures bien adaptes pour le rglement des oprations. L'avenir appartient aux systmes de rglement transfrontires qui, sur les plans de la scurit et de l'efficacit, rpondent  des normes aussi leves que celles des systmes nationaux. C'est ainsi, et seulement ainsi, qu'il sera possible de matriser les risques systmiques. Des systmes de rglement performants constituent en outre une condition  remplir pour parvenir  une concurrence loyale entre les places financires. Des efforts en vue d'accrotre l'efficacit des systmes de rglement sont en cours sur le plan mondial. Le systme TARGET ("Trans-european Automated Real-time Gross settlement Express Transfer"), qui assurera le trafic des paiements en euros, entrera bientt en service dans l'UE. Les banques suisses exploiteront en commun un tablissement (la "Swiss EURO Clearing Bank", SECB) qui oprera  Francfort-sur-le-Main, avec la technologie du SIC, et les raccordera ainsi indirectement  TARGET. Pour ses oprations en euros, la Banque nationale recourra elle aussi aux services de la SECB. En ouvrant le SIC  des organismes de clearing trangers et  d'importants acteurs qui oprent  l'tranger sur les marchs, la Banque nationale peut contribuer  la mise en place d'infrastructures plus fiables de rglement. Elle soutient le projet CLS ("Continuous Linked Settlement") des grandes banques commerciales. Ce projet ambitieux vise  liminer les risques de rglement dans les oprations de change. La Banque nationale est vivement intresse  ce qu'une connexion efficace soit tablie avec le SIC, le systme de paiement en francs suisses. Les critres rgissant l'accs au SIC ont t adapts pour tenir compte de telles volutions. Des entreprises communes et des organismes de clearing oprant sur le plan international (CLS notamment), ainsi que les banques qui y participent, peuvent en principe accder  distance au SIC, pour autant qu'il en rsulte une rduction des risques systmiques ou un renforcement de la place financire suisse. Il faut galement que les bnficiaires de cet accs  distance soient soumis, en matire de surveillance bancaire et de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent,  des rgles au moins aussi strictes que celles qui sont en vigueur en Suisse. L'accs  distance est dj ralis pour les membres allemands d'EUREX, la Bourse des produits drivs. Il est ouvert galement aux membres de la Bourse Suisse qui oprent de l'tranger. Enfin, l'accs  distance au SIC sera ouvert aux acteurs trangers du march des pensions de titres en francs suisses,  partir du printemps 1999, quand l'tape "Repo International" sera ralise. Pour tre accept, le participant devra toutefois satisfaire, du ct des titres, aux exigences requises par le principe "livraison contre paiement". Il devra donc ouvrir un dpt  la SEGA, la Socit suisse pour le virement de titres SA. Grce  ces infrastructures, il sera possible de passer des oprations de politique montaire avec des contreparties  l'tranger. Dans cette optique, des obligations d'Etat, libelles dans d'importantes monnaies trangres, seront incluses elles aussi dans le panier des titres que la Banque nationale a dfini pour ses oprations de pension. Le panier sera largi ds qu'un rglement efficace "livraison contre paiement" sera assur. La Banque nationale ne risque-t-elle pas, aprs l'ouverture du SIC, de perdre le contrle du march montaire? Cette crainte n'est pas justifie. Les avoirs en comptes de virements resteront pour nous pleinement transparents. De surcrot, les participants trangers ne dtiendront que peu d'avoirs en comptes de virements en fin de journe, tant donn qu'ils n'ont pas  satisfaire, en francs suisses,  des dispositions en matire de liquidits. Nous sommes persuads que ces deux ouvertures  davantage de contreparties et davantage de titres admis en pension  sont de nature  renforcer le march montaire en francs suisses et  rendre plus efficace la mise en uvre de la politique montaire.

Title: Introductory Remarks, End-of-year Media News Conference, Zurich
text: Year-end press conference, Zurich, 11 December 1998 Introductory remarks by Jean-Pierre Roth, Vice-Chairman of the Governing Board of the Swiss National Bank In recent months, the financial difficulties encountered by some Asian countries, then Russia, and the risks of destabilization of South America, have led to the establishment of financial assistance actions and initiated a discussion on a possible reform of the rules of operation of the international monetary system. Turbulence in emerging economies Many have seen in these crises tremors caused by deregulation and the globalization of markets. It is because of the globalization of markets, they say, that such large funds have been able to invest in emerging economies, and it is because of the high mobility of capital that they have been able to withdraw from them, placing some of them in serious difficulties by contagion. In our opinion, it is important here not to confuse cause and effect. The free movement of capital in the markets is not at the origin of the crises that have erupted; nevertheless, it has dramatically revealed situations of imbalance and provoked rapid and profound adjustments. At the heart of the problem were the lack of foresight on the part of local authorities and the speculative behaviour of donors. Indeed, emerging countries' access to the international capital market, greatly facilitated by liberalization, has often led these countries to easy solutions, with high long-term risks. In addition, some of them have encountered difficulties in organizing their economic system. In particular, the ineffective supervision of the banking and financial sectors and the maintenance of exchange rate regimes that no longer correspond to the underlying fundamental factors are regrettable. Without an effective regulatory framework and a coherent conception of economic policy, their openness to capital movements entailed the danger of financial weakening. The most extreme example of a "two-speed" society, where business dynamism rubbed shoulders with paralysis of the social framework, was Russia, whose financial collapse could only surprise those who forgot that sustainable economic development is compatible only with a properly organized civil society. To the improvidence of the authorities, we must oppose the lightness of the decisions of those who have allowed themselves to be blinded by high yields and by attractive prospects for development. Often, investors have imagined having an explicit or implicit public guarantee. The unilateral moratorium decreed by the Russian authorities has created a new situation in this regard. International cooperation The situation in Asia and Russia could not leave the International Monetary Fund indifferent, and this in two respects. First, the IMF's mission is to support the structural reform efforts of its members. Secondly, the Monetary Fund must endeavour to prevent other countries, already in a fragile situation, from being threatened by excessive reaction by the markets. As a result, the IMF had to pursue a delicate policy of pressure and support aimed both at helping countries in difficulty - without rewarding their "laissez-faire" - and at protecting those who might have become the object of massive withdrawals of funds in a market whose risk appetite was clearly diminishing. It is in response to these various objectives that the Fund - supported by the industrialized countries - has come to the aid of the Asian countries, Russia and Brazil. In each of these cases, the Swiss National Bank provided assistance. direct or indirect. In the case of Korea, we have committed, alongside 11 other countries, to open a line of credit to this country in the event that the means made available to it by the IMF prove insufficient. Our commitment in this regard amounted to 312.5 million. In the Russian case, our participation has increased at 526 million of Dollars either 6% of the 8.8 billion credit allocated to the IMF by the G10 countries under the General Agreements Borrowing (EBIT), this credit mechanism that allows them to make resources available to the Fund additional when the latter is experiencing an insufficient state of liquidity. Finally, in the case of Brazil, we expressed our readiness to supplement IMF credit by contributing 250 million to an internationally coordinated effort of 14.5 billion. In addition, we have agreed, through an activation of the New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB)  a newly created credit facility to strengthen THE EFAs  to allocate 633 million to the International Monetary Fund so that it has sufficient liquidity to finance its credit. Currently, the Swiss National Bank's participation in actions in favour of countries in balance of payments difficulties or in favour of the IMF amounts to CHF 2.6 billion. CHF 1.6 billion was granted through the activation of the GAB and THE NAB, chf 1 billion is committed to bilateral actions under the Federal Decree on Switzerland's cooperation in international monetary measures. For bilateral loans, the financial resources are made available by the SNB, but the credit risk is borne by the Confederation. The amounts made available by Switzerland for monetary assistance are therefore significant, but their reimbursement can be considered to be well insured. On the one hand, the advances granted to the IMF under the GAB and the NAB will be reimbursed by the new resources that the Monetary Fund will obtain on the occasion of the 11th quota review that will take place shortly. On the other hand, bilateral loans are not isolated actions of Switzerland but internationally coordinated operations, most often linked to an IMF programme, which gives them a high probability of repayment. Finally, it should be recalled that Switzerland has never had to suffer a default in this area and that its policy of allocating bilateral credits has been very prudent, not distinguishing itself from that of other small European countries (Belgium, Sweden, the Netherlands). With the allocation of a credit of 250 million dollars to Brazil, the commitment ceiling of 1 billion francs set in the federal decree since 1985 has been reached. Switzerland therefore no longer has room for manoeuvre with regard to bilateral monetary aid. This situation is unsatisfactory due, in particular, to our country's interest in the stability of the international monetary system and the importance of Switzerland's presence in emerging countries. If Switzerland wants to be able to continue to make its voice heard in international financial forums, it is important that it does not remain without means of action for long. We therefore hope that the Federal Council and Parliament will give favourable consideration to the question of raising the limit laid down in the Federal Decree. The Role of the IMF The difficulties encountered over the past twelve months by emerging economies have also led to a broad debate on the role of the Bretton Woods organizations in the new environment created by globalization and market liberalization. In our view, this new environment cannot call into question the strategy adopted so far by the Fund. However, adjustments must be made in order to make its action more effective. Today, as in the past, the pursuit of a stable macroeconomic policy is the responsibility of the countries concerned. International organizations can only play a monitoring, inciting and supportive role in this regard. Moreover, private operators - the markets - cannot be relieved of their responsibility to assess realistically the risks they incur. It is therefore less a question of adopting new rules than of applying known principles more carefully. Conditionality must remain the cornerstone of the allocation of Fund appropriations. Linking international assistance to the implementation of reforms is a necessity. If this conditionality has created difficult social situations, it is because the ability of emerging countries to adapt their structures to a liberal organization of markets has often been overestimated. A more realistic approach should allow for programmes that may be less ambitious, but better guarantee sustainable development. In terms of transparency, new emphasis could be defined. In this area, it is important to create a framework for market operators to better assess the situation of individual economies. More transparency about public external debt is desirable, but also more transparency in the IMF's judgements on the macroeconomic management of its members. With increased transparency, additional pressure will be exerted on the authorities in charge of macroeconomic policy. In a liberalized environment, the nature of the responsibility of international financial organizations is changing. In the future, it will be less a question of helping countries in difficulty with payments than of preventing the emergence of imbalances more vigorously. The stability of the international financial system depends first and foremost on the behaviour of the countries themselves, their compliance with financial discipline and the proper functioning of their internal supervisory mechanisms. International financial organizations will, as a matter of priority, have to ensure the right management of each; in this regard, they will be assisted by more transparent information on the financial situation of individual countries. With international organizations whose role would be more preventive than curative and a more transparent environment, the conditions will also be created for investment risks in emerging economies to be properly measured and fully borne by the private sector.
