Title: Focus on foreign exchange market and reference interest rates
text: Exposed Embargo until November 16, 2017, 6:30 p.m. Focus on the foreign exchange market and reference interest rates Aperitif "Money market" Dewet Moser Alternate Member of the Executive Board Swiss National Bank Geneva, 16 November 2017 , Zurich, 2017 He thanked Mirjam Baumberger, Basil Guggenheim, Alain Kouo, Peter Kuster, Barbara Stahel, Singh Surya and Jan Thomer for their valuable contribution to the drafting of this presentation, as well as the Language Services of the SNB. Page 1/7 Ladies and gentlemen In my turn, I am pleased to welcome you, once again, to the "Money Market" aperitif organized in Geneva by the Swiss National Bank (SNB). Andrea Maechler has just shown us, on the one hand, how currency purchases and the negative interest rate have enabled the SNB to prevent the Swiss franc from appreciating further. On the other hand, it highlighted the effects of the negative interest rate on the Swiss franc bond market and on credit operations. The Swiss franc has weakened in recent months. The monetary policy measures taken by the SNB have certainly contributed to this development. So today I can join you in welcoming the normalization that is taking place in the foreign exchange market. However, we are aware that the Swiss franc is still at a high level, that the situation can change rapidly in the markets and that we must therefore remain ready to act at any time and without delay. But this is another very important topic that I would like to address here first. This subject has been with us faithfully for some years: I am referring to the reform of reference interest rates. Here too, the context has changed a lot compared to 2016. The UK regulator announced in July 2017 that it would only support the publication of Libor until the end of 2021. The wide acceptance of Libor on the market makes this rate effective... Libor is by far the best established rate in Switzerland. For decades, the Libor-based swap curve has been used as a reference for the pricing and valuation of Swiss franc bonds and loans. My first slide illustrates these relationships in a stylized way. The curve reflects developments in the interest rate swap market. On this market, for the different durations, variable rate payments are exchanged for fixed rate payments and vice versa. The curve shows the fixed rates for the different durations. In Switzerland, Libor is used as a variable rate and thus serves as the basis for the swap curve. In transactions involving the Swiss franc, the swap market is much more liquid than the bond or loan market. This curve therefore serves as a reference for price formation on the Swiss credit and capital market. An investigation by the SNB showed that the Libor and the swap curve based on this rate serve as the basis for pricing four out of five Swiss franc loans (transparent 2). Because of this importance, Libor also naturally presents itself as a reference rate in the field of derivatives, particularly for hedging purposes. The nominal volume of Libor-based contracts is estimated at around CHF 6 trillion, or about ten times Switzerland's gross domestic product (GDP). Swap contracts certainly account for a large part of this volume. The relatively high liquidity of the derivatives market in turn reinforces the benchmark function of the swap curve for pricing. This interaction between pricing on the capital market and the use of derivatives on the market has Page 2/7 contributed to the importance of Libor as a "common denominator". This importance is such that this rate has become almost unavoidable for market participants, although in some cases another reference rate would in fact be more appropriate from an economic point of view. This high dependence of financial markets on an indicator should not be a problem in itself as long as this rate is credible and robust. This has generally been the case in recent decades, and the common standard of Libor has increased the efficiency of markets. However, with the financial crisis, the volume of unsecured money market transactions declined dramatically and has never since recovered. However, this market serves precisely as a basis for calculating libor. This phenomenon, it must be stressed, does not concern only the franc, but all currencies. ... but complicates its abandonment and replacement It is in this context that the United Kingdom announced that its authorities would stop, at the end of 2021, to support the various Libor panels. This decision reveals the disadvantages of the heavy dependence on Libor. Indeed, the abandonment of Libor represents a difficult task, which can only be controlled collectively by market players. Each of them must contribute to an orderly transition by confronting this issue without delay and proceeding in a coordinated manner. Various working groups accompany and steer the process. In Switzerland, the National Working Group on CHF reference rates (NWG) is in charge of the file. This working group is composed of representatives of banks and other specialists in the financial industry. The SNB is also participating in the reform by chairing with a representative of the private sector and managing the technical secretariat of the NWG. Since the revelation in 2012 of Libor's manipulations, the international community, under the aegis of the Financial Stability Board, has worked intensively towards a reform of reference interest rates. In a common learning process, administrators, market participants and authorities have reached important conclusions. First, it is imperative to involve the markets and obtain their approval in the reform process. To be convinced, just think of the many long-term contracts that refer to Libor, and for which a solution must be found. Second, a clear governance structure, transparently determining the allocation of tasks and responsibilities, is needed to ensure that benchmark rates are credible and robust. Thirdly, international requirements for reference interest rates, the IOSCO principles, must be respected. And fourthly, the transition must be coordinated between the different players so that the change of reference takes place smoothly throughout the market. Other currency areas are also evaluating alternatives to Libor (transparent 3). Here you can see the progress of the work on an international scale. This development leads to a replacement of libor by an overnight interest rate. Page 3/7 This may relate to the pledged or unsecured money market; the difference is usually minimal due to short maturities. In Switzerland, the NWG recommended at its October session that the Swiss Average Rate Overnight or SARON, which is based on the repo market, be used to succeed Libor. It has set up two sub-groups to study the use of SARON, one in the field of retail credit and the other in the field of wholesale derivatives. Our country has the advantage of having well-known and well-established indices, the Swiss Reference Rates (SRR), and in particular the SARON. Since their launch by SIX Swiss Exchange and the SNB in 2009, they have been available as reference values for the pledged money market (transparent 4). SARON is already serving as an alternative in another transition process that market participants are facing. It replaces the TOIS fixing, which will cease to be published at the end of this year. Swaps whose floating rate leg relates to SARON instead of TOIS fixing were made as early as April 2017. SARON is based on a solid calculation basis, formed by the transactions concluded and the quotations that can lead to a day-to-day transaction. This segment is the most liquid segment of the repo market against swiss francs. With a view to replacing THE TOIS fixing, SIX Swiss Exchange, as administrator of the SRRs, has also set up a committee to study the subject. This committee of experts shall provide advice and assistance. It brings together representatives of the Stock Exchange, SIX Repo, which is responsible for setting rates, the SNB and the most important market players. In addition, SARON meets the principles of IOSCO. To summarize its advantages in a single sentence, SARON is based on a broad base, offers a true picture of the market and presents a standardized, transparent and therefore understandable method of calculation. In addition, this method is subject to continuous evaluation to determine whether it remains appropriate in the light of possible structural changes in the market. In Switzerland, the NWG is taking the lead in the transition process. The SNB, which has been involved in the Swiss franc money market for many years, will continue to support this process closely by providing an interface function. We publish on our website the main documents relating to the progress of the reforms, and in particular the minutes of the NWG meetings (transparent 5). You will also find more information on RRSs. I would like to close the subject of reference rates by appealing to you as market participants. Because the responsibility for choosing the reference rate to replace Libor and for the process of orderly transition lies with the private sector. Even if the end of libor is not quite sealed yet, you must have in mind that it will no longer be available to you after 2021. Use this delay to determine how affected you are by the disappearance of libor. Stable and reliable reference rates are essential for the proper functioning of modern financial markets. That is why I advise you to prepare in time for the transition and change, to actively share your concerns in this process and to read the lines Page 4/7 guidelines issued by the NWG. I am confident that in this way we will achieve our goal of a well-ordered change in the benchmark interest rate without any problems. The weakening of the Swiss franc is based on a broad base in the foreign exchange market Let me now turn to the subject of the foreign exchange market. The latter has also seen significant developments in recent months. From the SNB's perspective, the great novelty is that the Swiss franc is no longer under strong upward pressure, at least for the time being. I would like to take a brief look back here to answer some of the questions that underlie the current context. What factors have set the stage for the weakening of the Swiss franc this summer? Under what market conditions has this weakening taken place? And what about the quality of the market? As we held our last money market aperitif in Geneva, the divergence between the two major currencies was increasingly marked. The euro was trading at a low level, which weighed on the franc. On the other side of the Atlantic, the election of Donald Trump as President of the United States had stimulated the dollar, which had stabilized the value of the franc weighted by foreign trade (transparent 6). The euro began to strengthen in mid-2017. This increase resulted in a considerable weakening of the US franc and dollar, in trade-weighted terms. Between the beginning of April and the end of June, the European currency gained 5 index points. Monetary policy alone cannot explain this reversal. Indeed, its orientation was already different on both sides of the Atlantic a year earlier. And as we know, this situation has not changed. Markets are expecting the U.S. Federal Reserve (Fed) to raise rates again. Conversely, the European Central Bank said three weeks ago that it wanted to maintain its expansionary monetary policy for the next nine months. Two other factors are better than monetary policy in explaining the turnaround in the foreign exchange market. First, the political uncertainty, which had made the euro unattractive, faded after the elections in France. Second, strong economic developments in the euro area have allayed fears about the fragility of the recovery. GDP has grown by more than 2% in the last three quarters, and economic sentiment indicators have continuously improved to levels they have not reached in recent years. In short, the upward pressure on the Swiss franc has subsided as the situation and climate have improved in the euro area, the economy has continued to develop favourably in the United States, and the health of the global economy has remained robust overall. To illustrate the peculiarity of the recent weakening of the Franc, it is necessary to examine a broader historical context, as presented in Slide 7. You've probably seen this chart in other presentations. It represents the evolution of the franc in terms weighted by foreign trade, from the beginning of 2011. Each square corresponds to Page 5/7 a four-week trading period. The color indicates the volume of transactions carried out on the foreign exchange market. A blue square indicates that the volume of transactions was relatively low during the period under review. A bright red square marks a period during which this volume has reached peaks. The chart can be considered as a trend indicator for the franc. The bright red color predominated in the summer of 2011 before the introduction of the floor price, then in the summer of 2012 and towards the end of 2014. During all these phases, the Swiss franc has come under strong upward pressure. The dark red square in summer 2017 represents an unusual phenomenon in the series of peaks observed in relation to the volume of operations: for the first time, an extremely high volume coincided with a weakening of the franc. Interest in a weaker franc was clearly high and enjoyed a broad base among market participants. A closer look shows the surprising intensity with which the rise in the euro and dollar franc rates was, for the most part, concentrated on a few days at the end of July. We see, in transparent 8, that the blue star, but especially the red star, have moved away from the point cloud. This chart shows, on a daily basis, how volume and volatility behave relative to the "normal level" represented by the zero line. The points are around the intersection of the two zero lines, and are very close to each other. The situation on the foreign exchange market is calm, it is not expected that news will fall. The exchange rate of the euro in the United States dollar and the exchange rates of the dollar and the euro in the United States have moderate trading differences, and operations concern modest volumes. Then, the prices of foreign currencies in francs begin to fluctuate. The volume and volatility of foreign exchange transactions dollar against franc (blue star) and especially euro against franc (red star) increase, which is reflected in the respective stars that move up and to the right: the franc is the subject of significant sales operations. These act as catalysts. Given these favourable circumstances, the franc is weakening. In a few days, the exchange rate of the euro in swiss francs rises from a level of around 1.10 francs to a level above 1.14 francs, which is reflected in significantly higher trading differences. Several technical levels are crossed, so that the dynamic is further strengthened. In the first week of August, the euro occasionally posted a rate of more than 1.15 francs. Depreciation dynamics do not affect market quality The weakening momentum of the Swiss franc observed in July 2017 was undeniably strong. It has certainly led to increased volatility in the exchange rate relationship. However, it did not affect the quality of the market. As shown in slide 9 using market quality indicators for the exchange rate between the euro and the Franc, activity has always remained steady. The location of the green dots on the vertical axis indicates that the daily spreads between best offers to buy and sell continued to decrease in the first half of 2017. These spreads widened significantly at the end of July, in line with the increase in volatility. However, the differences observed after the reversal of the exchange rate are not of concern: Page 6/7 they are in line with long-term averages and signal that the quality of the market is still good. It is interesting to also look at the size and gradient of green dots. These two elements reflect the frequency of large price fluctuations. The smaller the size of the dot and the paler the hue, the smaller the price variations. In July, the dots were small and pale. The depreciation of the Swiss franc clearly took place without sudden changes in prices and in a market whose quality remained intact. All these observations confirm the previous observation that the weakening of the Franc rests on a broad basis. However, it is likely that many market participants, especially those who were counting on a unilateral allocation of risk in transactions against francs, were surprised by the events. Let us dare to sketch a perspective for the future. To what extent has the recent weakening of the Swiss franc affected analysts' expectations of the market? Transparent 10 reflects a clear observation: the magnitude and speed of the depreciation of the franc also surprised analysts. The real spot price comes out of the blue margin. This represents the breakdown of analysts' forecasts for a quarter. At the end of each quarter, exchange rate expectations for the following quarter are recorded. After being caught off guard, analysts are now assuming that the weakening of the franc is a lasting phenomenon. They are therefore revising their forecasts upwards. The red dash curve, which represents the median of current expectations for the end of the year, stands at a level above CHF 1.15 per euro. The range formed by the red lines, however, indicates a strong dispersion. After a phase of greater volatility, the gap between expectations has again widened considerably. The renewed tension between North Korea and the United States last August reminded market participants that the franc was still considered a safe haven. While the situation on the foreign exchange market has eased somewhat, it remains fragile. In this context, our expansionary monetary policy, which is based on maintaining the negative interest rate and our willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market if necessary, remains appropriate. The SNB remains present on the foreign exchange and money market markets in order to fulfil its mandate. We continue to carefully observe, analyze and interpret facts, trends and structural changes. Now, I invite you all to continue our discussions over a drink. Thank you for your attention, your interest and your contribution to the proper functioning of financial markets. The presidency is carried out jointly by a representative of the private sector and a representative of the Swiss National Bank (SNB). The NW G is open to representatives of the ba nques as rciales (resident or non-resident) and to specialists from other sectors of finance. The banca ires stables which are not yet represented are the bienven us. The Federal Financial Market Surveillance Authority (FINMA) is invited as an observer. On spring 20 16, the NW G is looking into the quest for the replacement of the TO IS fixing by SARON with a view to the sustion of the TOIS fixi ng at the end of 2017. At its meeting on 5 October 20 17 it recommended saron to finance the Libor for the franc. The SNB supports national and international efforts to reduce the reference rates of Switzerland, it thus exercises the presidency of the NWG co nj ointemen t with a representative of the private sector. The NWG's recommendations are not sociological. The decisions on recommendations are taken by a simple majority of the votes expressed in the same way. The provision of reference interest is a matter for operators in the markets, the SNB refrains from the scrutiny and above all the role of arbitrator. It also organises the technical secretariat of the NW G and helps to organise meetings. As such, it makes available the section on its website for the publication of the procedures of this working gro upe and other documents relating to the reform process. Il a form deux sous-groupes chargs dtudier le recours au SARON, lun dans le domaine des crdits (retail) et lautre dans celui des produits drivs (wholesale). Notre pays prsente lavantage de disposer dindices connus et bien tablis, les Swiss Reference Rates (SRR), et en particulier le SARON. Depuis leur lancement par SIX Swiss Exchange et la BNS en 2009, ils sont disponibles comme valeurs de rfrence pour le march montaire gag (transparent 4). Le SARON sert aujourdhui dj de solution de rechange dans un autre processus de transition auquel les acteurs du march sont confronts. Il vient en effet remplacer le TOIS fixing, qui cessera dtre publi  la fin de cette anne. Des swaps dont la jambe  taux variable se rapporte au SARON au lieu du TOIS fixing ont t passs ds avril 2017. Le SARON repose sur une base de calcul solide, forme par les oprations conclues et les cotations pouvant aboutir  une transaction au jour le jour. Ce segment est le plus liquide du march des pensions de titres contre francs. Dans la perspective du remplacement du TOIS fixing, SIX Swiss Exchange a, en tant quadministrateur des SRR, galement constitu une commission charge dtudier le sujet. Ce comit dexperts assume des fonctions de conseil et dassistance. Il runit des reprsentants de la Bourse, de SIX Repo qui est charge dtablir les taux, de la BNS et des acteurs les plus importants du march. De plus, le SARON rpond aux principes de lOICV. Pour rsumer ses avantages en une seule phrase, le SARON repose sur une large assise, offre une image fidle du march et prsente un mode de calcul standardis, transparent et donc comprhensible. Par ailleurs, cette mthode fait lobjet dune valuation continue visant  dterminer si elle reste adapte compte tenu dventuels changements structurels du march. En Suisse, le NWG assume la direction dans le processus de transition. La BNS, qui sinvestit depuis de nombreuses annes dj en faveur du march montaire en francs, continuera daccompagner ce processus de prs en assurant une fonction dinterface. Nous publions sur notre site les principaux documents relatifs  lavancement des rformes, et notamment les procs-verbaux des sances du NWG (transparent 5). Vous y trouverez aussi de plus amples informations sur les SRR. Jaimerais clore le sujet des taux de rfrence en vous lanant un appel, en tant quacteurs du march. Car la responsabilit du choix du taux de rfrence appel  remplacer le Libor et du processus de transition ordonne revient au secteur priv. Mme si la fin du Libor nest pas encore tout  fait scelle, vous devez avoir en tte quil ne sera plus  votre disposition aprs 2021. Utilisez ce dlai pour dterminer dans quelle mesure vous tes concerns par la disparition du Libor. Des taux de rfrence stables et fiables sont primordiaux pour le bon fonctionnement de marchs financiers modernes. Cest pourquoi je vous conseille de vous prparer  temps  la transition et au changement, de faire part activement de vos proccupations dans ce processus et de prendre connaissance des lignes Page 4/7 directrices mises par le NWG. Je suis convaincu que de cette manire, nous atteindrons sans encombres notre but,  savoir un changement bien ordonn du taux dintrt de rfrence. Laffaiblissement du franc repose sur une large assise au niveau du march des changes Permettez-moi  prsent daborder le sujet du march des changes. Ce dernier a lui aussi connu des dveloppements significatifs au cours des derniers mois. Dans loptique de la BNS, la grande nouveaut rside dans le fait que le franc nest plus soumis  de fortes pressions  la hausse, du moins pour le moment. Jaimerais jeter ici un bref regard en arrire afin de rpondre  certaines questions qui sous-tendent le contexte actuel. Quels facteurs ont prpar le terrain  laffaiblissement du franc cet t? Dans quelles conditions du march cet affaiblissement a-t-il eu lieu? Et quen est-il de la qualit du march? Au moment o nous tenions notre dernier apritif du march montaire  Genve, la divergence entre les deux grandes monnaies tait de plus en plus marque. Leuro se ngociait  un faible niveau, ce qui pesait sur le franc. De lautre ct de lAtlantique, llection de Donald Trump  la prsidence des Etats-Unis avait stimul le dollar, ce qui avait stabilis la valeur du franc pondre par le commerce extrieur (transparent 6). Leuro a commenc  se renforcer au milieu de 2017. Cette progression sest traduite par un affaiblissement considrable du franc et du dollar des Etats-Unis, en termes pondrs par le commerce extrieur. Entre dbut avril et fin juin, la monnaie europenne a gagn 5 points dindice. La politique montaire ne permet pas dexpliquer  elle seule ce renversement de tendance. En effet, son orientation tait dj diffrente de part et dautre de lAtlantique un an auparavant. Et comme on le sait, cette situation na pas chang. Les marchs sattendent  ce que la Rserve fdrale des Etats-Unis (Fed) relve de nouveau les taux. A linverse, la Banque centrale europenne a dclar il y a trois semaines vouloir maintenir sa politique montaire expansionniste pour les neuf prochains mois. Deux autres lments parviennent mieux que la politique montaire  expliquer le revirement observ sur le march des changes. Premirement, lincertitude politique, qui avait rendu leuro peu attrayant, sest estompe aprs les lections en France. Deuximement, lvolution conjoncturelle solide de la zone euro a dissip les craintes concernant la fragilit de la reprise. Le PIB a affich une croissance suprieure  2% lors des trois derniers trimestres, et les indicateurs de climat conomique se sont continuellement amliors pour sinscrire  des niveaux quils navaient plus atteints ces dernires annes. En bref, la pression  la hausse subie par le franc est retombe, car la situation et le climat se sont amliors dans la zone euro, la conjoncture a continu dvoluer favorablement aux Etats-Unis, et la sant de lconomie mondiale est reste robuste dans lensemble. Pour illustrer la particularit de laffaiblissement rcent du franc, il faut examiner un contexte historique plus vaste, tel quil est prsent dans le transparent 7. Vous avez probablement dj vu ce graphique dans le cadre dautres exposs. Il reprsente lvolution du franc en termes pondrs par le commerce extrieur,  partir de dbut 2011. Chaque carr correspond  Page 5/7 une priode de ngoce de quatre semaines. La couleur indique le volume des oprations effectues sur le march des changes. Un carr bleu signifie que le volume des oprations tait relativement faible lors de la priode considre. Un carr rouge vif marque une priode pendant laquelle ce volume a atteint des pics. Le graphique peut tout  fait tre considr comme un indicateur de tendance pour le franc. La couleur rouge vif prdominait en t 2011 avant lintroduction du cours plancher, puis en t 2012 ainsi que vers fin 2014. Pendant toutes ces phases, le franc a subi de fortes pressions  la hausse. Le carr rouge fonc en t 2017 reprsente un phnomne insolite dans la srie des pics observs en rapport avec le volume des oprations: pour la premire fois, un volume extrmement lev a en effet concid avec un affaiblissement du franc. Lintrt port  un franc moins fort tait manifestement grand et a bnfici dune large assise auprs des acteurs du march. Un examen plus dtaill montre lintensit surprenante avec laquelle la hausse des cours de leuro et du dollar en franc sest, en grande partie, concentre sur quelques jours fin juillet. On voit, dans le transparent 8, que ltoile bleue, mais surtout ltoile rouge, se sont loignes du nuage de points. Ce graphique montre, sur une base journalire, comment le volume et la volatilit se comportent par rapport au niveau normal reprsent par la ligne zro. Les points se situent autour de lintersection des deux lignes zro, et sont trs proches les uns des autres. La situation sur le march des changes est calme, il nest pas prvu que des nouvelles tombent. Le cours de leuro en dollar des Etats-Unis ainsi que les cours du dollar et de leuro en franc affichent des carts de ngoce modrs, et les oprations portent sur des volumes modestes. Puis, les cours des monnaies trangres en franc commencent  fluctuer. Le volume et la volatilit des oprations de change dollar contre franc (toile bleue) et surtout euro contre franc (toile rouge) augmentent, ce qui se traduit par les toiles respectives qui se dplacent vers le haut et vers la droite: le franc fait lobjet doprations de vente importantes. Celles-ci jouent le rle de catalyseur. Compte tenu de ces circonstances favorables, le franc saffaiblit. Le cours de leuro en franc passe en quelques jours dun niveau denviron 1,10 franc  un niveau suprieur  1,14 franc, ce qui se reflte dans des carts de ngoce nettement plus levs. Plusieurs niveaux techniques sont franchis, de sorte que la dynamique se renforce encore. Lors de la premire semaine daot, leuro affiche par moments un cours suprieur  1,15 franc. La dynamique de la dprciation naffecte pas la qualit du march La dynamique daffaiblissement du franc observe en juillet 2017 tait incontestablement forte. Elle a certes entran une volatilit accrue au niveau de la relation de change. Cependant, elle na pas affect la qualit du march. Comme le montre le transparent 9  laide dindicateurs relatifs  la qualit du march pour le cours entre leuro et le franc, lactivit est toujours reste rgulire. Lemplacement des points verts sur laxe vertical indique que les carts enregistrs quotidiennement entre meilleures offres dachat et de vente ont continu  diminuer au premier semestre 2017. Ces carts se sont sensiblement creuss fin juillet, en relation avec laccroissement de la volatilit. Les carts observs aprs le renversement de tendance concernant le cours de change ne sont toutefois pas proccupants: Page 6/7 ils sont conformes aux moyennes observes  long terme et signalent que la qualit du march est toujours bonne. Il est intressant dexaminer en outre la taille et le dgrad des points verts. Ces deux lments refltent la frquence de fortes fluctuations des cours. Plus la taille du point est petite et plus la teinte est ple, plus les variations de cours sont faibles. En juillet, les points taient petits et ples. La dprciation du franc sest manifestement droule sans variations brusques des cours et sur un march dont la qualit est reste intacte. Toutes ces observations confirment la constatation faite prcdemment,  savoir que laffaiblissement du franc repose sur une large assise. Il est pourtant probable que de nombreux acteurs du march, notamment ceux qui tablaient sur une rpartition unilatrale du risque dans les oprations contre francs, aient t surpris par les vnements. Osons esquisser une perspective davenir. Dans quelle mesure laffaiblissement rcent du franc a-t-il influ sur les anticipations des analystes concernant le march? Le transparent 10 traduit un constat clair: lampleur et la rapidit de la dprciation du franc ont aussi surpris les analystes. Le cours au comptant rel sort de la marge bleue. Celle-ci reprsente la rpartition des prvisions tablies par les analystes pour un trimestre. A chaque fin de trimestre, les anticipations relatives aux cours de change pour le trimestre suivant sont enregistres. Aprs avoir t pris au dpourvu, les analystes partent dsormais de lhypothse que laffaiblissement du franc est un phnomne durable. Ils revoient donc leurs prvisions  la hausse. La courbe en tirets rouges, qui reprsente la mdiane des anticipations actuelles portant sur la fin de lanne, stablit  un niveau suprieur  1,15 franc pour un euro. La fourchette forme par les lignes rouges indique cependant une forte dispersion. Aprs une phase de plus grande volatilit, lcart entre les anticipations sest de nouveau creus considrablement. Le regain de tension entre la Core du Nord et les Etats-Unis en aot dernier a rappel aux acteurs du march que le franc tait toujours considr comme une valeur refuge. La situation sur le march des changes sest certes dtendue quelque peu, mais elle reste fragile. Dans ce contexte, notre politique montaire expansionniste, qui repose sur le maintien du taux dintrt ngatif et sur notre disposition  intervenir au besoin sur le march des changes, demeure approprie. La BNS reste prsente sur le march des changes et sur le march montaire, afin de pouvoir remplir son mandat. Nous continuons dobserver, danalyser et dinterprter minutieusement les faits, les tendances et les changements structurels. A prsent, je vous invite tous  poursuivre nos discussions autour dun verre. Je vous remercie de votre attention, de votre intrt et de votre contribution au bon fonctionnement des marchs financiers. Title: Remarks by Thomas Jordan on the acquisition of a majority stake in Landqart AG
text: Zurich, 21 December 2017 Thomas Jordan Remarks by Thomas Jordan on the acquisition of a majority stake in Landqart AG We would like to inform you that, yesterday, the Swiss National Bank acquired 90% of the shares in Landqart AG. The remaining 10% of the share capital will be taken over by Orell Fussli Holding. The vendor is a subsidiary of the Canadian-based company Fortress Paper Ltd. As a manufacturer of security paper, Landqart, located in Landquart, Graubunden, produces the Durasafe substrate used for the new Swiss banknote series. In addition to the acquisition of Landqart AG, Landqart Management and Services was also purchased, and also in the same ratio. Landqart Management and Services holds the patents for the Durasafe technology. Today, we will be explaining the background to this transaction and the rationale behind it. After that, we will be happy to answer your questions. The SNBs new ninth-series banknotes are based on a substrate which is developed and produced by Landqart  the Durasafe substrate. This substrate subsequently goes to Orell Fussli for printing and to have the various security features added. Landqart is the only company to provide the Durasafe technology and associated production capabilities. In October, Landqart informed us that a major customer of conventional banknote paper  i.e. not of the Durasafe substrate  had unexpectedly cancelled its order at short notice. Losing this order meant that projected fourth-quarter turnover dropped by 16%. For 2018, this will even mean as much as 30%. Landqart was thus facing a liquidity crisis which it was not able manage alone. In an initial move, on 2 November, Landqart applied for short-time working for a period of three to four months starting in December, and it informed its staff and the local media accordingly. At the same time, it also began to look for a long-term solution. Meanwhile, the Page 1/2 Zurich, 21 December 2017 Thomas Jordan problem facing the SNB was that the manufacture of the substrate for the ninth banknote series would not have been guaranteed across the entire production stream. After considering various options, the SNB came to the conclusion that, under the circumstances, the best solution would be to join forces with Orell Fussli and take over Landqart together. We subsequently entered into negotiations with Fortress, which culminated yesterday in the signing of contracts and the acquisition of both companies. The purchase price for Landqart AG and Landqart Management and Services amounts to CHF 21.5 million. Of this, the SNBs portion amounts to CHF 19.35 million. Owing to the liquidity situation at Landqart, restructuring measures and an injection of liquidity will have to be initiated. This acquisition enables the SNB to fulfil its statutory mandate of ensuring the continued supply of cash. Had the production of Durasafe not been safeguarded, issuance of the new banknote series would have been jeopardised. The SNB did not want to take this risk. The takeover of Landqart not only means acquiring the patents and production units, it also means securing the expertise and commitment of Landqarts employees. This in turn ensures that the production process can be continued without interruption. In view of the current orders situation, short-time working will have to be continued. An indepth analysis of the future business model will show which further restructuring measures are necessary. Rest assured that Landqarts management and the new owners will do everything possible to secure new orders. However, the market for banknote paper is very competitive. There are two reasons for cooperating with Orell Fussli in the takeover of Landqart:  First, Orell Fussli is Landqarts direct contracting partner for the supply of the Durasafe substrate.  Second, Orell Fussli has the requisite industrial know-how and is the SNBs general contractor for the new banknote project. As the new owners, the SNB and Orell Fussli will appoint the new boards of directors, while the existing executive board will look after the operational management. In the first phase, Landqarts liquidity will have to be secured, the company put on a sound footing, and the production of Durasafe guaranteed. This is being provided for by the takeover of Landqart and the planned rapid injection of liquidity by the new owners. In the second phase, a comprehensive situation review and a strategy review will need to be conducted. We are therefore currently not in a position to discuss options resulting from this phase. We will now be happy to answer your questions. Page 2/2

Title: Spotlight on SNB profits and shares
text: Speech Embargo 27 April 2018, 10.00 am Spotlight on SNB profits and shares 110th Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders of the Swiss National Bank Jean Studer President of the Bank Council Swiss National Bank Berne, 27 April 2018 Page 1/6 Dear Shareholders Ladies and Gentlemen Dear Guests I am sure you will remember the headlines from the beginning of the year. Titles like SNB in the money, double manna from the SNB and SNB makes the cantons happy. They were of course alluding to our record profit for the 2017 financial year. However, in forming an opinion about this result, it should be borne in mind that the SNBs mandate requires it to act in the interests of the country as a whole, rather than focusing on returns. In the first part of my speech I will therefore discuss our annual result, explain how it came about and how the profit is used. In the second part, I will take a closer look at the ownership of our shares and the characteristics of our institution as a special-statute joint-stock company. My motivation in doing so is the soaring price of the SNB share over the past few months, a development that has surely not escaped your attention. In this connection, I would like to remind you, as shareholders, of the features of the SNB share. How profits arise and how they are used First, let me address the question of why the SNB has been able to post record high profits of CHF 54 billion for 2017. As you know, our foreign exchange reserves have grown substantially in recent years in the wake of monetary policy measures taken to combat the strong Swiss franc, specifically as a result of foreign currency purchases. At the end of 2017, these foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately CHF 744 billion. The SNB invests its foreign currency in broadly diversified asset classes and currencies. In the past year, the Swiss franc weakened markedly, particularly against the euro, and global stock markets boomed. We benefited from these favourable developments, with exchange rate and share price gains contributing CHF 43 billion to our result. In addition, interest and dividend income totalled CHF 13 billion. Taking into account price movements in bonds, which produced a loss of CHF 6 billion on the back of rising interest rates, foreign currency positions posted a profit of almost CHF 50 billion. A CHF 3 billion valuation gain on gold holdings and CHF 2 billion income from negative interest on sight deposits held at the SNB also contributed to the result. This shows that the reported profit is largely a valuation gain on investments at the end of the financial year. Let me once again stress that the SNBs overarching goal is not to generate maximum profits. Rather, management of our currency reserves serves the requirements of monetary policy. This means that the SNB must ensure that it is able to expand or reduce the balance sheet at any time, if monetary policy so requires. At the same time, however, management of our assets should also preserve the value of our currency reserves. Our annual result depends heavily on movements in exchange rates, the capital markets and the gold price. This also means that the result can fluctuate widely. Not only is a very high profit possible, as in 2017, but also a heavy loss. Given the vast expansion in the foreign exchange reserves in recent years, even small exchange rate variations lead to substantial Page 2/6 fluctuations in earnings. The expansion of the balance sheet has therefore also increased the risks, a fact that is taken into account in profit distribution. This leads me to the question of how the profit for 2017 will be distributed. There has been no shortage of suggestions as to how it could be deployed. Since Januarys announcement of an unusually high profit, a range of proposals have been put forward from various parties. It is completely understandable that such a large sum of money should capture the imagination and be eyed with eager anticipation. However, as I mentioned earlier, the SNB has no room for manoeuvre in this area. The National Bank Act (NBA) specifies clearly and conclusively how the profits are to be allocated. The purpose of these provisions is to preserve the SNBs capacity to act in the long term. The current environment shows just how important this is. The fulfilment of its monetary policy mandate has led, as I mentioned earlier, to a huge expansion in the balance sheet, which increases risk exposure. The SNB must be able to bear these risks, now and in the future. This is why the annual result is used, first, to top up the provisions for currency reserves. The provisions are the most important component of the SNBs equity capital and must be maintained at the level required by monetary policy considerations. The allocation to the provisions is based on the performance of the Swiss economy, with the level being determined by the nominal GDP growth rate. However, the allocation must correspond to a minimum of 8% of total provisions at the end of the previous year, in order to ensure that the balance sheet is strengthened even in periods of low nominal GDP growth. Just such a minimum allocation was applied in 2017, boosting the provisions by CHF 5 billion. The portion of the annual result remaining after allocation to the provisions for currency reserves represents the distributable profit. Together with the distribution reserve (that is the earnings or losses of the previous year brought forward), it constitutes the net profit/net loss. If a net profit has been achieved, a dividend not exceeding 6% of the share capital is paid out in accordance with the NBA. For the 2017 financial year, the maximum dividend of CHF 15 per share will be paid out. One-third of any net profit remaining after the distribution accrues to the Confederation, and two-thirds to the cantons. On the basis of the current agreement between the Federal Department of Finance and the SNB, the Confederation and the cantons receive a total of CHF 2 billion for 2017. The remainder of the profit is allocated to the distribution reserve. The distribution reserve, which now stands at CHF 68 billion, serves as a buffer to help smooth the SNBs profit distributions to the Confederation and the cantons from year to year. The rules for the profit distribution and the associated policy on provisions have proved their worth. They are aimed at ensuring a solid capital base and thus help the SNB to retain its room for manoeuvre in fulfilling its monetary policy mandate over the long term. Equally, the rules permit surplus capital to be paid out to the Confederation and the cantons over time. Page 3/6 SNB shares and share ownership Let me now turn to my second topic, one that is likely to be of particular interest to you as shareholders, the SNB share. Before addressing recent share price movements, let me first look at the breakdown of our shareholdings from a slightly longer-term perspective, as this too reflects the special nature of our institution. Our shareholder base has remained remarkably stable over succeeding decades. Since the SNB was founded in 1907, the cantons have held almost 40% of share capital. The cantonal banks (formerly issuing banks) hold nearly 12%. Altogether, public sector shareholders held over half of the SNB shares at the end of 2017. The other half was in the hands of private shareholders, although because of the restriction on voting rights, which I will address later, their voting power was just under 24%. The voting rights of the cantons and cantonal banks, as well as other public authorities, specifically municipalities, thus came to over 76%. Since the beginning of the 1990s, private shareholders have also included foreign shareholders. At the end of 2017, they held 10% of the share capital and their share of voting rights was 3.1%. Where there has been a change, though, is in the proportion of shares that has not been entered in the share register. This rose again in 2017, reaching almost 22% at the end of the year; ten years ago it was just 14%. We do not know who the owners of these shares are, and they are also unable to attend our general meeting, which of course is regrettable. It would be preferable if these shareholders registered their holdings and the number of unregistered shares did not rise further. The Confederation is not a shareholder. Since the SNB serves the general public, both the Constitution and Swiss legislation grant the Confederation participation and supervision rights, without the need for it to hold shares. They include the right of the Federal Council to appoint the majority of Bank Council members (six of eleven), among them the president and vice president. It is also the Federal Councils responsibility to appoint the three members of the SNB Governing Board, including the chairperson and vice chairperson, and the three deputy members (all based on the Bank Councils recommendation). Moreover, the SNB is obliged to submit its financial report to the Federal Council for approval before it can be adopted by the General Meeting of Shareholders. Now let me shift perspective and turn to the increase in the SNB share price observed since mid-2017, in particular. Whereas share prices have occasionally fluctuated quite considerably in the past, this latest rise has been so sharp that it has attracted a good deal of attention and triggered some speculation as to the potential causes. Even though the SNB refrains, in principle, from commenting on its share price performance, I am fully aware that this current movement may raise questions. I am therefore taking the rise in the share price as an opportunity to remind you of some particular and generally known features of both the SNB share and shareholders rights at the SNB. Since the foundation of the SNB, its legal form has been that of a special-statute jointstock company. This combines elements from private and public law. While the public-law Page 4/6 component expresses the SNBs mandate to act in the interests of the country as a whole, the private element helps to ensure its independence. As far as the provisions of company law are concerned, they only apply unless otherwise specified in the NBA. Compared to shareholders in other joint-stock companies, the participatory and property rights of SNB shareholders are heavily restricted. Participatory rights are limited in that the general meeting of shareholders can only elect five of the eleven members of the Bank Council. Furthermore, shareholders voting rights are limited to a maximum of 100 shares, with the exception of Swiss public-law corporations and cantonal banks. The property rights restrictions include the NBAs explicit provisions on the appropriation of profit as discussed earlier. The level of the dividend is also defined in the NBA; it may not exceed 6% of the share capital. As we have seen, even a high profit in the preceding year does not change this. The reason for this limitation in the dividend is that SNB profits are not generated from the deployment of share capital but from the fact that the SNB has the noteissuing privilege (in other words, the exclusive right to issue banknotes), and fulfils a public mandate. Profits, therefore, do not accrue primarily to the shareholders but to the public sector. The same applies to the assets. In accordance with art. 32 of the NBA, even in the event of the SNBs liquidation shareholders would have no right to its assets. The wording of the dispatch on the NBA amendment of June 2002 clearly indicated that this explicit regulation in the article on liquidation is also important with respect to stock market trading: It helps to reduce the likelihood of speculative overvaluation of SNB shares as occasionally occurs on the basis of misunderstandings regarding the rights of SNB shareholders. Finally, it is worth mentioning in this context that the question of buying out private shareholders came up during the consultation phase for the new NBA. After thorough examination, the idea was rejected and no amendment was made. To date, there has been no change in this position. As I said before, the elements I have just outlined will all be very familiar to you. However, I thought it appropriate, in the light of our share performance, to bring them to your attention once again. Concluding remarks A central bank should be judged by its success in fulfilling its mandate, which is to conduct a monetary policy serving the interests of the country as a whole. In just a minute, the Chairman of the Governing Board, Thomas Jordan, will explain how the SNB fulfilled this mandate in 2017. From my perspective, I would once again like to emphasise that the SNBs specific public mandate makes it a distinctive institution. Unlike other companies, the level of its profits is no indicator of how successfully it has fulfilled its mandate. In fact, in the interests of the country as a whole, it may be necessary to make loss-making monetary policy decisions. Thus, the Page 5/6 annual result can fluctuate widely. It is therefore essential that the SNB is appropriately equipped and adheres to its prudent policy on provisions. Last years exceptionally high profit is no reason to waver from this approach, quite the contrary. Given the size of our balance sheet, it is particularly important to preserve the SNBs capacity to act in the long term. The special-statute joint-stock company legal form means that SNB shares are unlike other shares. They are subject to certain restrictions on shareholder rights imposed by law. This bespoke legal form offers our institution an appropriate framework so that it can fulfil its mandate as effectively as possible with the necessary independence. However, the special character of SNB shares means that they are less a conventional investment than a means for shareholders to express their solidarity with our institution. On behalf of the entire Bank Council, I would like to take this opportunity to thank you for your support, your loyalty and especially for your participation in todays general meeting. Let me also thank the Governing Board for an excellent working relationship, which has always been productive and rewarding. Lastly, I would like to pay tribute to the SNBs staff who work tirelessly in the service of our institution. Page 6/6

Title: Introductory remarks, news conference
text: Berne, 21 June 2018 Andrea M. Maechler Introductory remarks by Andrea M. Maechler I will begin my remarks with an overview of the situation on the financial markets, before giving an update on the status of the reforms regarding reference interest rates. And in closing I would like to say a few words about our branch office in Singapore, which is celebrating its fifth anniversary. Situation on the financial markets Let me start with the developments on the financial markets. The first half of 2018 was characterised by a return of volatility on the markets, as well as price movements shaped by the continuing normalisation of monetary policy in the US. The higher volatility followed a prolonged phase of exceptionally low levels, and was driven by the marked correction on global equity markets in February. Furthermore, uncertainty has repeatedly been fuelled by concerns over increasing global trade conflicts and mounting geopolitical tension. The most pronounced fluctuations were to be found on the equity markets, whereas the impact on risk sentiment in other asset classes was modest (cf. chart 1). In the second quarter, the focus shifted increasingly to concerns regarding the euro area, with risk premia rising considerably at times amid the difficulties in forming a government in Italy and the vote of no confidence held in Spain. At regional level, various asset classes were affected by a flight to safe havens. However, the situation has calmed down again slightly of late with the formation of a new government in Italy. Contagion effects at the global level remained relatively limited. As the tightening in US monetary policy continued, the divergence between the US Federal Reserves stance and that of the central banks in the other advanced economies became more pronounced. This also influenced developments on the global financial markets. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries rose markedly, and in April climbed back above 3% for the first time Page 1/6 Berne, 21 June 2018 Andrea M. Maechler since 2014. The interest rate differential between the US and the euro area thus widened: while yields in the US reflected the positive momentum in the economy, economic data in the euro area were slightly weaker and, together with increased political uncertainty, this weighed on government bond yields. Although the reversal in interest rates in the US initially had a relatively modest impact on emerging economies, the markets in these countries have come under pressure in the first half of this year as a result of the stronger US dollar and the rise in long-term interest rates in the US. In certain countries, risk premia were additionally pushed higher by macroeconomic and political factors. Against this backdrop, the performance on global equity markets was mixed. In the US, the S&P 500 was able to more than recoup the losses suffered in the first quarter, and has gained around 3% in the year to date. It was buttressed in particular by US companies continuing to post solid earnings growth in the first three months of the year. In Europe and Asia, following an interim correction, the increase in uncertainty in the euro area and the renewed escalation of the trade dispute between the US and China has recently weighed on share prices. The Euro Stoxx 600 and Japans Nikkei thus lost around 2% each. Given the high weighting of defensive stocks, the broad Swiss equity market index, the SPI, had previously been unable to profit to the same degree from the recovery in risk sentiment, and remains down around 5% (cf. chart 2). At the beginning of the year, the foreign exchange market was dominated by the weakening of the US dollar, with a correction only coming in the course of the second quarter owing to markedly rising US interest rates. The euro was initially largely stable until impacted by weaker economic data in the euro area and political uncertainty surrounding the formation of a government in Italy. Given the heightened uncertainty worldwide, the yen was in demand and appreciated as a result (cf. chart 3). The situation on the global financial markets is currently somewhat volatile again. The Goldilocks environment for the markets that was still prevailing at the start of 2018  namely stable economic momentum coupled with low inflation rates and persistently low financial market volatility  has deteriorated slightly over the past six months in light of the aforementioned events. Political developments, increasing protectionist tendencies and challenges arising from the ongoing normalisation of monetary policy in the advanced economies have the potential to trigger further tension on the global financial markets. Status of reference interest rate reforms I would now like to address the progress that has been made with regard to reforming reference interest rates. Since the UK Financial Conduct Authority announced nearly a year ago that it would not guarantee the continuation of Libor beyond 2021, there have been increasing efforts at both international and national levels to find a replacement. The key forum in this respect in Switzerland is the National Working Group on Swiss Franc Reference Interest Rates, which is open to representatives from all major stakeholders such as banks and other financial market participants as well as their respective industry associations. In October Page 2/6 Berne, 21 June 2018 Andrea M. Maechler 2017, the working group recommended the Swiss Average Rate Overnight (SARON) as the alternative to the Swiss franc Libor. The primary focus at present is on the implications of the changeover to SARON for the derivatives and capital market and the loan and deposit market. SARON has already gained in importance as a reference interest rate, and now forms the basis of a corresponding yield curve. Although the outstanding volume on the newly established Overnight Index Swap (OIS) market, which uses SARON, is still modest, it has been rising steadily in recent months. Going forward, this curve could serve for the pricing of Swiss franc loans, as is currently the case with Libor. This would improve the environment for replacing Libor. All market participants must ensure that they are well prepared for the probable discontinuation of Libor from the end of 2021. Responsibility for a smooth transition lies with the private sector. Among the issues to be resolved are the treatment of existing Libor-linked contracts and the design of SARON-referenced products. The SARON yield curve should also be developed further, with more players participating in this market segment. These challenges should thus be prioritised accordingly. This also means that viable solutions must be developed quickly and the necessary framework established. The SNB will continue to support the efforts of the National Working Group in a coordinating role, while also running the latters technical secretariat.1 Singapore branch office celebrates fifth anniversary In closing, I would now like to say a few words about our branch office in Singapore. At our in June 2013, the SNB announced that its newly opened Singapore office would commence operations the following month. Five years on, this is a good opportunity for us to take stock. Singapore is the SNBs first and only branch office outside Switzerland. The team currently has nine members of staff, and their primary task is to ensure the efficient management of the SNBs currency reserves in the Asia-Pacific region. It is well known that the SNBs currency reserves have risen substantially as a result of the monetary policy measures aimed at countering the strength of the Swiss franc. We therefore felt it appropriate to expand our investment universe, in particular also in the high-growth region of Asia. The portfolio managers at our Singapore branch now manage bonds and stocks worth some CHF 90 billion, the key investments being denominated in yen, Australian dollars, South Korean won, Chinese renminbi and Singapore dollars. Having a presence in Asia is also highly beneficial when it comes to implementing monetary policy on the foreign exchange market. Currency trading is known for being a round-theclock business with no such thing as opening hours. Our branch in Singapore is able to ensure 1 Further information is available on our website at . Page 3/6 Berne, 21 June 2018 Andrea M. Maechler the seamless continuation of foreign exchange market coverage when it is night in Switzerland. Having a local SNB presence in Asia has also proved to be very advantageous with regard to monitoring and analysing developments on the financial markets. This provides us with a deep understanding of the market and economic environment in the Asia-Pacific region, which is becoming ever more significant for the global economy.
